A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #24089: kubectl validation fails when creating a non-v1 object in a v1 list

Issue description:
In other words, you can't create/replace/delete/apply deployments with kubectl if they're in a list.

Works as expected:

``` console
$ cat nginx-rc.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: List
items:
  - apiVersion: v1
    kind: ReplicationController
    metadata:
      name: nginx
    spec:
      replicas: 1
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            name: nginx
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: nginx
              image: nginx
$ kubectl create -f nginx-rc.yaml
replicationcontroller "nginx" created
```

Does not work as expected:

```
$ cat nginx-dpl.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: List
items:
  - apiVersion: extensions/v1beta1
    kind: Deployment
    metadata:
      name: nginx
    spec:
      replicas: 1
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            name: nginx
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: nginx
              image: nginx
$ kubectl create -f nginx-dpl.yaml
error validating "nginx-dpl.yaml": error validating data: couldn't find type: v1beta1.Deployment; if you choose to ignore these errors, turn validation off with --validate=false
$ kubectl create -f nginx-dpl.yaml --validate=false
deployment "nginx" created
```

This is a high priority issue for us, since it means we can't (easily) use apply (or any kubectl command) with lists of JSON objects since we've moved all our replication controllers over to deployment objects, which is hampering the UX of our config efforts.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #25484: Weird quota and limitrange behavior

Issue description:
I'm using HEAD in the master branch with a simple 1 master + 1 slave setup. API server is started with the following flag: `--admission-control=LimitRanger,NamespaceLifecycle,ResourceQuota`.

To reproduce:

```
kubectl create namespace test
kubectl --namespace=test create -f docs/admin/resourcequota/quota.yaml
kubectl --namespace=test create -f docs/admin/limitrange/limits.yaml
kubectl --namespace=test run nginx --image=nginx:latest --requests="cpu=500m,mem=100mi"
```

Of course, no pods will be created because "cpu=500m" exceeds the default value of "cpu=300m". This is expected behavior. However, the unexpected part is when I do a `kubectl describe namespace test`, and the cpu usage was showing:

```
Resource Quotas
 Name:          quota
 Resource       Used    Hard
 --------       --- ---
 cpu            1500m   20
 memory         300Mi   1Gi
```

As each container was supposed to request 500m cpu, this looks like replicaset controller is trying to create more pods after previous ones were rejected, and this causes the quota usage to keep increasing. This will continue until the quota controller runs and reconciliates the actual information (by default it runs every 5 minutes). I'm wondering if this is the intended behavior, as this could cause all the quota to be used up very quickly until the quota controller runs the next time, and effectively, this blocks all the future pod creation.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: pod constraints func for quota validates resources

This prevents quota from prematurely charging for quota usage around a pod when the pod had invalid resources.  For example, if a container limit < container request, prior to this a quota would charge the usage, but the pod failed validation.

We do not do full validation on the pod because at this point, the pod does not have all of ObjectMeta filled out.

PR title: use monotonic now in TestDelNode
PR description:

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #27062: Downward API for resource specification should default to node capacity when limits are not set.

Issue description:
As of now the downward API for resource specification defaults to `0` for `limits` when `limits` are not specified in the pod spec. This behavior is not ideal for applications.
What does a limit of `0` mean?
In reality, not having a limit translates to being limited by node capacity as of now, and node allocatable in the future once it is enforced.
We should default to node capacity instead of setting `limit.memory` to `0` when `limits` are not set.
And for `limits.cpu` we should again default to node capacity and allocatable in the future.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #27378: nsenter mount gets doesn't list the right mounts, causing containerized kubelet unable to detach cloud disk

Issue description:
In nsenter_mounter, [List()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/util/mount/nsenter_mount.go#L161) reads mounts from `/rootfs/proc/mounts`. Because `/proc/mounts` is sym link to `/proc/self/mounts` and the containerized kubelet usually bind mount host rootfs in slave mode, thus containerized kubelet's mounts is different from what host sees.

This causes kubelet unable to umount/detach volumes.

The right way to do is to read hosts's proc, i.e. `/rootfs/proc/1/mounts`

@kubernetes/sig-storage

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #27582: node e2e test teardown crashes with nil deref if node services could not be started

Issue description:
In `/test/e2e_node/e2e_node_suite_test.go`, the node services are started in the `BeforeSuite` logic. If they fail to start, ginkgo's `Fail` function is called, which ultimately initiates test tear down and thus the `AfterSuite` logic in the same file.

The `AfterSuite` logic calls `e2es.stop()` (defined in `test/e2e_node/e2e_service.go`), which will try to e.g. `es.stopService(es.kubeletCmd)`, where `es` is the `e2eService` and `kubeletCmd` is the `*killCmd` for the kubelet service.

Unfortunately, because the service failed to start, this pointer is nil, and we get a nil pointer dereference in the `Kill` function (in `test/e2e_node/e2e_service.go`).

Off the top of my head, I see two potential solutions to this problem.
1. Pre-allocate default `killCmd` structs on the `e2eService` struct created in the `newE2eService` function in `test/e2e_node/e2e_service.go`. We could just make `killCmd.cmd = nil` on these, because the assumption appears to be that if `killCmd.cmd == nil`, the service is not running. (It appears that prior to the addition of `killCmd`, a nil `cmd` was interpreted as 'service not running,' and that this `cmd` field got rolled into `killCmd`, see 66d74f969dbbde894949b87366d215e020167faf).
2. Or, simply add an additional check to the `Kill` function, where we assume that if the `killCmd` is `nil`, the respective service is not running.

Thoughts? I want to make sure I'm not missing something here.

@timstclair because you added teardown code in 66d74f969dbbde894949b87366d215e020167faf
@euank because you added `killCmd` in 34996f1b84104a83033fb62cec72ec86f9eef8c1

Note: Tim is on vacation so I'm not really expecting a response from him.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #24254: Amazon ELBs - ICMP and Network Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU)

Issue description:
The firewall rules created on Amazon ELBs do not include ICMP. This means that issues can occur with PMTU. Please see below for more information.

When a HTTP/TCP request exceeds a certain payload size, with ELBs not allowing "ICMP request/reply", the request stalls. This is due to the ELB trying to send big packets to the client but the client dropping them since the MTU was higher than expected.

To avoid this ICMP traffic should be allowed on the ELB so they can negotiate the MTU:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Path_MTU_Discovery
- http://www.networkworld.com/article/2224654/cisco-subnet/mtu-size-issues.html
- http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/network_mtu.html

When enabling ICMP traffic the client will be able to communicate with the ELB normally.

An example of what occurs when ICMP is not enabled.

```
$ time curl -v -O > /dev/null http://a8222e4ee025111e6a25d0a91ac3ee4d-1379358768.eu-west-1.elb.amazonaws.com/docs-api/swaggerui/lib/jquery.slideto.min.js

* Connected to a8222e4ee025111e6a25d0a91ac3ee4d-1379358768.eu-west-1.elb.amazonaws.com (52.49.165.25) port 80 (#0)
> GET /docs-api/swaggerui/lib/jquery.slideto.min.js HTTP/1.1

100   369  100   369    0     0     12      0  0:00:30  0:00:29  0:00:01    85
* Connection #0 to host a8222e4ee025111e6a25d0a91ac3ee4d-1379358768.eu-west-1.elb.amazonaws.com left intact

real    0m29.547s
user    0m0.012s

```

Ideally security rules for ELBs should be allowed to be attached to an ELB via annotations and/or by default.

ICMP rules at a minimum to avoid this should cover:
- 0 - Echo Reply
- 8 - Echo Request

*\* Please note that this does not just affect Amazon ELBs, but in addition direct access to instances too.**

Issue description:
This came up while I was working on #25977, for which I am adding support to run clusters with the master on GCI and nodes on Debian. Issue #28515: kube-dns v15+ cannot set verbosity

Issue description:
When replacing kube-dns v11 (as defined w/ the v1.2.4 release) with v15 in the v1.3.0 release, we notice that the `skydns` container inside the `kube-dns` pod is overly verbose. This appears to be due to an inability to turn of `Info` logging within [dns.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/dns/dns.go#L583). Neither the `--v` flag, nor the `--stderrthreshold=2` flags appear to have any impact. On a 65 node cluster with approximately 1700 pods, this results in a log load of over 10,000 log entries per second. Can we implement a mechanism to turn off Info-level logging from kubedns?

See also CoreOS kubernetes issue [555](https://github.com/coreos/coreos-kubernetes/pull/555#issuecomment-229530165).

### Issue Summary
Currently CIDRAllocator observes only Node creations and deletions. When Node is created it tries to assign a CIDR to it. If it fails for any reason (no available CIDRs, run out of Node update retries) it won't ever retry, as the Node won't be "created" again. We need to add a mechanism for retrying assignments in such cases.

A repository contains the following reported issue: Issue #29358: GCE PD Detach fails if node no longer exists Issue description: **Problem:** If a node with a GCE PD attached is deleted (before the volume is detached), subsequent attempts by the attach/detach controller to detach it continuously fail, and prevent the controller from attaching the volume to another node. **Repro steps:** 1. Create a pod referencing a GCE PD 2. Wait for pod to get scheduled and running. 3. Delete the node VM (using gcloud) that the pod is scheduled to. 4. From `/var/log/kube-controller-manager.log`: ``` I0721 03:21:43.464087 7 reconciler.go:134] Started DetachVolume for volume "X" from node "Y" due to maxWaitForUnmountDuration expiry. messages.content: A repository contains the following reported issue: Issue #30792: Add Encryption to dynamic provisioner Issue description: ## Summary Encrypted volumes is a commonly requested feature for Kubernetes storage and requirements exist downstream to use encrypted volumes. The following is a summary of the three cloud providers that allow dynamic provisioning and the current state of volume encryption for each. **_TL;DR:_**  Add encryption support for EBS PersistentVolumes. AWS has optional encryption and allows key via the API. GCE encrypts volumes by default but does not allow user-defined keys in the API. GCE allows custom keys via manual volume creation in the UI.  Cinder volumes can be manually created w/ encryption. @kubernetes/sig-storage @abhgupta @thockin @saad-ali I'm going to follow up with a PR today/tomorrow to meet the 1.4 cutoff on Friday. ## Encryption by Cloud Provider ### AWS - AWS does _not_ encrypt volumes by default - AWS API allows an optional boolean flag for encryption - AWS API allows a user to specify which key to use for encryption with a default key provided by AWS if not specified. See: - [http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/AmazonEBS.html](http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/AmazonEBS.html) - [http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/EBSEncryption.html](http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/EBSEncryption.html) - [http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_CreateVolume.html](http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_CreateVolume.html) ### GCE - GCE encrypts all volumes by default - Users can provide their own keys, but this is a manual step in the UI only. - GCE API does _not_ provide a way to specify which key should encrypt which disk - Volume attachment to the node requires the same key it is encrypted with. This is a manual step in the UI only. See: - [https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/customer-supplied-encryption](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/customer-supplied-encryption) - [https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/reference/latest/disks/insert](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/reference/latest/disks/insert) ### Cinder - No encryption by default - No opt-in encryption via API - Block storage can be optionally encrypted - Manual creation of the volumes is required See: - [https://wiki.openstack.org/wiki/VolumeEncryption](https://wiki.openstack.org/wiki/VolumeEncryption) - [http://docs.openstack.org/mitaka/config-reference/block-storage/volume-encryption.html](http://docs.openstack.org/mitaka/config-reference/block-storage/volume-encryption.html) - [http://docs.openstack.org/juno/config-reference/content/section_create-encrypted-volume-type.html](http://docs.openstack.org/juno/config-reference/content/section_create-encrypted-volume-type.html) ## Proposed Workflow: 1. Admins create however many keys in AWS as they wish. This is a manual step. 2. Admins create StorageClasses with the fully-qualified AWS resource name for the key. Implementation details: - Add encryption support to AWS cloud provider - Add encryption support to Kubernetes EBS volume plugin - Use StorageClass for both the Encrypted boolean and EncryptionKeyName in PV controller A pull request was created to resolve it: PR title: Add encryption to EBS dynamic provisioner PR description: Resolves https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/30792 Adds encryption to the EBS cloud provider and provisioner. Details: - we are starting image-pullers from manifest files on all nodes - at some point they are finishing - if there are enough of them, some of them will be garbage collected by "pod-garbage-collector" - kubelet receives DELETE/REMOVE event about this pod, e.g. ``` I0907 09:30:41.545069 3657 kubelet.go:2312] SyncLoop (DELETE, "api"): "e2e-image-puller-e2e-test-wojtekt-minion-group-ekar_kube-system(328a7913-74dd-11e6-8d6e-42010af00002)" I0907 09:30:41.579395 3657 config.go:281] Setting pods for source api I0907 09:30:41.579886 3657 kubelet.go:2306] SyncLoop (REMOVE, "api"): "e2e-image-puller-e2e-test-wojtekt-minion-group-ekar_kube-system(328a7913-74dd-11e6-8d6e-42010af00002)" ``` - once the pod is removed, kubelet starts sending "GET" requests for this pod every 10s and getting 404 errors - this happens infinitely This clearly looks like a bug - Kubelet should simply forget about this pod and stop sending those requests. messages.content: A repository contains the following reported issue: Issue #31765: Node E2E: stop-services option not working properly. Issue description: In node e2e, we have the `stop-services` option to keep the services running after test for further debug. messages.content: A repository contains the following reported issue: Issue #29155: E2E & Node E2E: Add image white list Issue description: For https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/29081. With https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/28807, we are going to share some tests between e2e and node e2e. However, one problem is that e2e and node e2e have different image prepulling. When adding a test which needs an new image, it's pain to add the image in both of them. And both of them are hard to maintain. Mostly, people just didn't realize they've introduced an new image, and even though, the test can still pass in most cases. This causes issues like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/28868. To avoid this, we should add an image white list. Only images in the white list could be used in the test. Because all pods should be created via [`CreatePod`](https://github.com/Random-Liu/kubernetes/blob/e40e82bd5c724675c26ca03a631171ecf6305cac/test/e2e/framework/pods.go#L46) in the future, we can do some check in it to make sure all images are in the whitelist. If we can make sure that all images are successfully pulled before test, we can even set the `ImagePullPolicy` to `Never` for all pods. This could be easily achieved in node e2e test framework, because we already have a similar white list in the test infrastructure. However, for regular e2e, the image list is hard coded in the [spec of static pod `e2e-image-puller`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cluster/saltbase/salt/e2e-image-puller/e2e-image-puller.manifest#L30). To achieve this, we need to change it to a `DaemonSet` and do some other walkaround. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/26110 @yujuhong /cc @kubernetes/sig-node A pull request was created to resolve it: PR title: Node E2E: Add image white list PR description: This is part of #29081. Fixes #29155. As is discussed with @yujuhong in #29155, it is difficult to maintain the prepull image list if it is not enforced. This PR added an image white list in the test framework, only images in the white list could be used in the test. If the image is not in the white list, the test will fail with reason: ``` Image "XXX" is not in the white list, consider adding it to CommonImageWhiteList in test/e2e/common/util.go or NodeImageWhiteList in test/e2e_node/image_list.go ``` Notice that if image pull policy is `PullAlways`, the image is not necessary to be in the white list or prepulled, because the test expects the image to be pulled during the test. Currently, the image white list is only enabled in node e2e, because the image puller in e2e test is not integrated with the image white list yet. /cc @kubernetes/sig-node --- This change is [](https://reviewable.kubernetes.io/reviews/kubernetes/kubernetes/32986) Merged upstream at: 2016-09-20T14:28:58Z PR size: +101 additions, -69 deletions, 16 files changed, 1 commits Analyze the issue and explain what problem it reports and how the linked pull request addresses it. messages.content: A repository contains the following reported issue: Issue #33984: CRI: garbage collection may remove just-created sandbox Issue description: Currently, kuberuntime removes a sandbox only when there are no containers belonging to it. But this introduces a potential problem of removing just-created sandbox, which means a sandbox may be removed if: - It has been created and hasn't become ready yet (which means `RunPodSandbox` has been requested and has no response, but the sandbox is already shown in `ListPodSandbox`) - garbage collection is run exactly at this time. The quick fix is adding age policy to sandbox, e.g. only remove a sandbox if it is older than X. But it doesn't really guarantee this won't happen theoretically (e.g.`RunPodSandbox` takes much longer than gc age). Maybe full gc policy should also be applied to sandboxes. @yujuhong @Random-Liu @yifan-gu What do you think? cc/ @kubernetes/sig-node A pull request was created to resolve it: PR title: Add sandbox gc minage PR description: Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/34272. Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/33984. This PR: 1) Change the `GetPodStatus` to get statuses of all containers in a pod instead of only containers belonging to existing sandboxes. This is because sandbox may be removed by GC or by users, kubelet should be able to deal with this case. 2) Change the CRI comment to clarify the timestamp unit (nanosecond). 2) Add MinAge for sandbox GC Policy. @yujuhong @feiskyer @yifan-gu /cc @kubernetes/sig-node --- This change is [](https://reviewable.kubernetes.io/reviews/kubernetes/kubernetes/34287) Merged upstream at: 2016-10-09T00:07:29Z PR size: +61 additions, -31 deletions, 7 files changed, 3 commits Analyze the issue and explain what problem it reports and how the linked pull request addresses it. messages.content: A repository contains the following reported issue: Issue #35498: Remove/replace pod.alpha.kubernetes.io/initialized annotation from petsets for beta Issue description: PetSets currently support an annotation `pod.alpha.kubernetes.io/initialized` in their PodTemplateSpec field. From the user documentation: > annotations: > pod.alpha.kubernetes.io/initialized: "true" > This field is a debugging hook. It pauses any scale up/down operations on the entire PetSet. If you’d like to pause a petset after each pet, set it to false in the template, wait for each pet to come up, verify it has initialized correctly, and then set it to true using kubectl edit on the pet (setting it to false on any pet is enough to pause the PetSet). If you don’t need it, create the PetSet with it set to true as shown. This is surprisingly useful in debugging bootstrapping race conditions. #### Use cases 1. **Debugging**: If one want to bring up the pets in my petset one after the other, while pausing after each step, confirming that the state is as expected, one may use this functionality. For example, a petset where each pet is a replica of a distributed database; we set the pod.alpha.kubernetes.io/initialized to `false` in the petset template initially. This leads to the following progression: - _PetSetController creates pet-0_ - Manually intervene and check that it has initialized as expected. - Set annotation to true (equivalent to marking that pet as healthy) - _PetSetController creates pet-1_ - Manually intervene and check that it has initialized as expected. - ... 2. **Blocking the PetSet controller**: - We may want to ensure that the petset controller is not performing scale operations when a different user-initiated action is in progress (for example, where pets are leaving due to a kubectl drain). - This may be used as a mechanism to orphan a pod from a petset controller (for a closer look), while ensuring that a replacement is not created. ## Beta plans The use case 1 above can be realized using `kubectl scale` and is probably easier to do that way rather than use the annotation. I don't see a reason to have that case supported when we can have users scale up a PetSet gradually and manually in an identical manner. It may have been of more importance before v1.4 when the scaler & reaper were not implemented. Due to the second use-case, if it would make sense to continue to have this ability, I propose that we move it from the PodTemplateSpec to the PetSetSpec, where it will eventually reside. This seems to me, like the logical place for such a debug hook to reside. In order to run/pause the scaling operations of the PetSet controller, we could have annotations along the lines of `stopSync: true/false` with the annotation defaulting to `false` when absent. /cc @erictune @kubernetes/sig-apps @smarterclayton A pull request was created to resolve it: PR title: Making the pod.alpha.kubernetes.io/initialized annotation optional in PetSet pods PR description: **What this PR does / why we need it**: As of now, the absence of the annotation `pod.alpha.kubernetes.io/initialized` in PetSets causes the PetSet controller to effectively "pause". Being a debug hook, users expect that its absence has no effect on the working of a PetSet. This PR inverts the logic so that we let the PetSet controller operate as expected in the absence of the annotation. Letting the annotation remain alpha seems ok. Renaming it to something more meaningful needs further discussion. **Which issue this PR fixes** _(optional, in `fixes #(, #, ...)` format, will close that issue when PR gets merged)_: fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/35498 **Special notes for your reviewer**: **Release note**: ``` release-note The annotation "pod.alpha.kubernetes.io/initialized" on StatefulSets (formerly PetSets) is now optional and only encouraged for debug use. ``` cc @erictune @smarterclayton @bprashanth @kubernetes/sig-apps @kow3ns The examples will need to be cleaned up as well I think later on to remove them. --- This change is [](https://reviewable.kubernetes.io/reviews/kubernetes/kubernetes/35739) Merged upstream at: 2016-11-02T16:58:00Z PR size: +16 additions, -10 deletions, 2 files changed, 1 commits Analyze the issue and explain what problem it reports and how the linked pull request addresses it. A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #40443: Bugs in docker 1.11 may stop kubelet from creating containers in the docker-CRI implementation

Issue description:
Forked from #34289.

In some cases, when docker (1.11.2) fails to create a container, it will not release the "name" associated with the container. kubelet can never create a container with the same name again. This phantom container cannot be listed or removed. The only way to release the name is to restart the docker daemon.

```console
$ sudo docker run --name=foo --security-opt=foo:bar busybox
docker: Error response from daemon: Invalid --security-opt 2: "foo:bar".
See 'docker run --help'.
$ sudo docker run --name=foo busybox
docker: Error response from daemon: Conflict. The name "/foo" is already in use by container 3f7fae9d56619c67cf1baa85bab8e649ef344931ccae385b3cec809bf79fe829. You have to remove (or rename) that container to be able to reuse that name..
See 'docker run --help'.
$ sudo docker rm foo
Error response from daemon: No such container: foo
$ sudo docker rm 3f7fae9d56619c67cf1baa85bab8e649ef344931ccae385b3cec809bf79fe829
Error response from daemon: No such container: 3f7fae9d56619c67cf1baa85bab8e649ef344931ccae385b3cec809bf79fe829
```

The [deferred cleanup function](https://github.com/docker/docker/blob/v1.11.2/daemon/create.go#L75) relies on the container id lookup, but the id (not the name) [hasn't been registered](https://github.com/docker/docker/blob/v1.11.2/daemon/create.go#L92) at the time of the [failure](https://github.com/docker/docker/blob/v1.11.2/daemon/create.go#L83-L90). This relevant code was refactored in docker 1.12+ and the bug was fixed.

Pre-CRI kubelet embeds a random string into the container name, so it'll always recover in this situation (i.e., no naming conflict). Now kubelet uses deterministic names for containers, this become a problem. The container will never be created. @Random-Liu wrote a script to scan the kubelet-cri-serial build logs and found that about ~7% of the builds ran into this problem.

We've discussed several fixes and decided to add a workaround in the `dockershim` package (note that it's not in kubelet because this is caused by a docker bug)
1. create a container
2. if it fails due to naming conflict, try removing the container
3. if the removal request fails with a "No such container" response, try creating a container with a `_randomstring` suffix appended to the name.
When parsing the name, dockershim will have to check if this suffix exists and trim them before returning to kubelet.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #33625: Esipp transition plan

Issue description:
Alpha to beta (1.5):
- Declare 2 sets of annotations, one in the alpha namespace (already exists) and one in the beta namespace (new)
- alpha always takes precedence
- If alpha is set to a valid value, we write the beta annotation to mirror it clobbering any user field

Why convert alpha to beta:
1. Users are auto transitioned
2. Not converting means if alpha and beta are set to 2 different values, deleting the alpha requires a cleanup of the alpha value, and an activation of the beta value. This might be confusing and error prone.
3. Not converting makes handling updates harder, as we would have to allow updates to the "inactive" one.

Beta to GA (1.6):
- Declare 2 fields that mirros the annotations in beta
- Ignore alpha annotations (any alpha annotations in play will continue to work because they were translated to the beta annotation)
- Perform the same conversion time clobbering

If users upgrade from 1.4 to 1.6 directly, the alpha annotation is ignored and esipp stops working.

```

**Environment**:
- **Cloud provider or hardware configuration**: `aws`
- **Install tools**: `kops` default install

**What happened**:
AWS EBS backed PersitantVolumeClaim created a volume in an AZ where there was a master but no nodes. Making it unusable.

**What you expected to happen**:
Zones with master and no nodes shouldn't be used to create the EBS Volume

**How to reproduce it** (as minimally and precisely as possible):
- AWS setup across 3 AZs in one region
- Master in three AZs
- Nodes in 2 AZs (so one AZ has a Master but no Nodes)
- Create a Storage class to use EBS without specifying AZ

```
kind: StorageClass
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1beta1
metadata:
  name: ebs
provisioner: kubernetes.io/aws-ebs
```
- Create PVC against StorageClass

```
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: data
  annotations:
    volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-class: "ebs"
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 8Gi
```
- PVC can create a volume in an availability zone with no nodes

**Anything else do we need to know**:
Mentioned on Slack channel #sig-aws with @justinsb who asked me to raise this

PR title: AWS: Skip instances that are taggged as a master

We recognize a few AWS tags, and skip over masters when finding zones
for dynamic volumes.  This will fix #34583.

This is not perfect, in that really the scheduler is the only component
that can correctly choose the zone, but should address the common
problem.

Issue #42929: pkg/util/flock.Acquire() doesn't guarantee mutual exclusion

Issue description:
**BUG REPORT**:

**Kubernetes version latest master**:

**Environment**:
- **Ubuntu 16.04 LTS, Linux 4.2.0-42-generic**:

**What happened**:
The `flock.Acquire()` doesn't provide mutual exclusion. Two processes can both grab the same flock at the same time.

**What you expected to happen**:
Only one process should be able to grab the flock.

**How to reproduce it** (as minimally and precisely as possible):

```shell
cat testflock.go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/util/flock"
)

func main() {
	if err := flock.Acquire("/tmp/foo.lock"); err != nil {
		fmt.Println("error:", err)
		return
	}

	fmt.Println("acquired")

	time.Sleep(time.Hour)
}

go build testflock.go; ./testflock
acquired

# open another terminal and run
./testflock
acquired
```

**Anything else we need to know**:

Although the flock doesn't work, the [watchForLockfileContention()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.7.0-alpha.0/cmd/kubelet/app/server.go#L324) does work. Since we _usually_ specify `--exit-on-lock-contention` together with `--lock-file`, so the 1st process will exit anyway.
However we still need to fix the flock..

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: pkg/util/flock: Fix the flock so it actually locks.
PR description:
With this PR, the second call to `Acquire()` will block unless the lock is released (process exits).
Also removed the memory mutex in the previous code since we don't need `Release()` here so no need to save and protect the local fd.

Fix #42929.

PR title: kubectl: fall back to computing QoS class if server does not populate
PR description:
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/42831

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/38989 changed how kubectl determines the the QoS Class field.  In order to prevent reimplementation of the QoS class logic in each client, the API server was modified to set the QoS Class in a new status field.  However API servers 1.5 and older do not set this field.  This results in a kubectl 1.6 client talking to a 1.5 API server to not print the QoS class field, which is a regression.

This PR causes kubectl to fall back to the old method of evaluting the QoS class when the status field from the API server is not set.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #43459: CVE-2017-1000056: PodSecurityPolicy admission plugin authorizes incorrectly

Issue description:
A PodSecurityPolicy admission plugin vulnerability allows users to make use of any PodSecurityPolicy object, even ones they are not authorized to use.

CVE: CVE-2017-1000056

* Fixed in [v1.5.5](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/releases/tag/v1.5.5) in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/7fef0a4f6a44ea36f166c39fdade5324eff2dd5e
* Fixed in release-1.5 branch in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/43491
* Fixed in master in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/43489

**Who is affected?**
Only Kubernetes 1.5.0-1.5.4 installations that do _all_ of the following:
* Enable the PodSecurityPolicy API (which is not enabled by default):
      `--runtime-config=extensions/v1beta1/podsecuritypolicy=true`
* Enable the PodSecurityPolicy admission plugin (which is not enabled by default):
      `--admission-control=...,PodSecurityPolicy,...`
* Use authorization to limit users' ability to use specific PodSecurityPolicy objects

kubeadm and GKE do not allow enabling PodSecurityPolicy in 1.5, so are not affected by this vulnerability.

kube-up.sh and kops do not enable PodSecurityPolicy by default, so are not affected by this vulnerability. A modified kube-up.sh or kops deployment could have enabled it.

**What is the impact?**
A user that is authorized to create pods can make use of any existing PodSecurityPolicy, even ones they are not authorized to use.

**How can I mitigate this prior to installing 1.5.5?**
1. Export existing PodSecurityPolicy objects:
      `kubectl get podsecuritypolicies -o yaml > psp.yaml`

2. Review and delete any PodSecurityPolicy objects you do not want all pod-creating users to be able to use (NOTE: Privileged users that were making use of those policies will also lose access to those policies). For example:
      `kubectl delete podsecuritypolicies/my-privileged-policy`

3. After upgrading to 1.5.5, re-create the exported PodSecurityPolicy objects:
      `kubectl create -f psp.yaml`

PR title: Include system:authenticated group when impersonating
PR description:
Fixes #43227

An authorized impersonation request solely for a specific username previously resulted in a `user.Info` that did not include either the `system:authenticated` or `system:unauthenticated` groups. Issue #43662: In-cluster config for kubectl cannot be disabled/overriden

Issue description:
I have an app running in a pod that shells out to kubectl. A kubeconfig file with credentials for four different clusters is included in the pod. However, kubectl always detects that it's being run from inside a cluster and uses the pod's cluster's apiserver instead of the credentials I'm explicitly passing it. I've tried various things to disable this detection and make it use the configuration I'm supplying, but it always uses the in-cluster configuration settings, which results in not only submitting to the wrong cluster, but this error being returned for many resources being applied:

```
the namespace from the provided object "foo" does not match the namespace "bar". You must pass '--namespace=foo' to perform this operation.
```

where "foo" refers to the resource I'm trying to create with `kubectl apply` (the namespace of the resource is in the input file) and "bar" is the namespace of the pod shelling out to kubectl. Running the exact same command locally works, because kubectl is not overriding what I pass it with in-cluster configuration.

Specifically, the command being run is:

```
kubectl --kubeconfig /path/to/.kube/config --context my-context apply -f resources.yml
```

I can't find any documentation on how to disable in-cluster config. I looked through the code of the Go client to try to figure out how it's choosing to do this. I tried various things to disable it, including:

* Setting the `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST` environment variable to an empty string, due to this: https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/49948ae0ca8eb31d632fbf346e25ee0eb6762d5b/tools/clientcmd/client_config.go#L505. But Kubernetes overrides my setting and fills in the environment variable like normal.
* Mounting an empty volume to /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount to try to prevent Kubernetes from mounting the service account files, but it mounts them anyway, overriding my explicit mount.
* Setting the `KUBECONFIG` environment variable to the path of the file I want it to use. It has no effect.

This is kubectl 1.5.x running in a Kubernetes 1.5 cluster. Notably, using kubectl 1.4.x does _not_ exhibit this behavior in the same Kubernetes 1.5 cluster. kubectl 1.4 works as expected.

Issue #42284: PodDisruptionBudget should use ControllerRef

Issue description:
Currently, PDB uses selector-based listers to determine which controller is managing a given Pod. Now that [ControllerRef](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/design-proposals/controller-ref.md) is implemented across all controllers that PDB looks at, the disruption controller should instead use the ControllerRef on a Pod (if any) to determine which controller manages the Pod.

Without this, PDB may look at the wrong controller(s), thus making the wrong decision about whether to allow an eviction. In the future, this may also allow PDB to respect ownership of Pods by controller types it doesn't know about (third-party controllers), as long as it can access the controller's `/scale` subresource.

Priority can take the range 1-10. Total priority for a node is sum of weight \* priority for each priority function, and the sum is accumulated into an int (see [PrioritizeNodes](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dae5ac482861382e18b1e7b2943b1b7f333c6a2a/plugin/pkg/scheduler/generic_scheduler.go#L227)). So obviously the total priority can overflow if someone sets the weight(s) too high.

The weights of all priority functions are compiled in (or specified in config file), so we can check to make sure maximum total priority can't overflow an int (take sum over all priority functions of 10 \* weight of that priority function, and make sure that's smaller than int(MaxUint >> 1) which according to StackOverflow is the way to find out what is max int (math package has max Int32, Int64, etc. but not max Int).

Note that scheduler extender is OK because although the policy runs in a separate process, the weight is specified in scheduler config file (ExtenderConfig struct) and the priority is bounded 1-10 as usual.

It is currently not possible to specify the desired FSType when using dynamically provisioned volumes. As I understand it, only a PV resource can specify the FSType. But as we don't create PVs by ourself when using dynamic provisioning, we have no chance to specify it.

I tried to understand the source when it comes to dynamic provisioning. As I understand it, the cloud specific VolumeSource (e.g. AzureDiskVolumeSource or AWSElasticBlockStoreVolumeSource) hold the desired FSType. I would suggest that  FSType should be added to either StorageClass or PersistentVolumeClaim. I'm not sure however which one would best fit, or if it fits at all.

PR title: deduplicate endpoints before DNS registration
PR description:
**What this PR does / why we need it**: Multizone clusters will return duplicated endpoints to the federation controller manager. ```
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"4", GitVersion:"v1.4.1+33cf7b9", GitCommit:"33cf7b9acbb2cb7c9c72a10d6636321fb180b159", GitTreeState:"not a git tree", BuildDate:"2016-10-13T15:13:44Z", GoVersion:"go1.7.1", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/amd64"}

```

**Describe *in detail* the feature/behavior/change you'd like to see.**

Currently `kubectl port-forward` only allows binding to localhost...

```
$ kubectl port-forward mypod 4560
Forwarding from 127.0.0.1:4560 -> 4560
Forwarding from [::1]:4560 -> 4560
```

It would be good to be able to bind to another local interface (and "all/*/0.0.0.0"), something like:

```
$ kubectl port-forward --bind-address 0.0.0.0 mypod 4560
Forwarding from 0.0.0.0:4560 -> 4560
Forwarding from [::]:4560 -> 4560
```

```
$ kubectl port-forward --bind-address 192.168.56.1 mypod 4560
Forwarding from 192.168.56.1:4560 -> 4560
```

This would allow more advanced interactions for debugging/interaction between local development environments and containers running on k8s.

[kubectl proxy](http://kubernetes.io/docs/user-guide/kubectl/kubectl_proxy/) supports `--bind-address` which seems like a good a name as any, to be consistent.

See also: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/25113

Issue description:
When collecting data for a projected volume, if an error is encountered, the plugin logs, but then continues setting up the volume and returns as if it were successful:

```
E0604 10:31:19.324314    3580 projected.go:265] Couldn't get configMap e2e-tests-projected-mnbzg/projected-configmap-test-volume-f1dfa503-4910-11e7-8d9d-0242ac110002: User "system:node:e2e-34198-minion-group-qnk2" cannot get configmaps in the namespace "e2e-tests-proj│

Issue #47077: HPA controller sends unecessary updates

Issue description:
**BUG**: the HPA controller submits updates every update interval, even if nothing has changed.  In clusters with large numbers of HPAs, as well as clusters with smaller HPA sync periods, this can cause an unnecessarily high volume of writes.

The HPA controller should only send updates if it actually has a change to the HPA status object.

metrics.

Issue #47012: incompatible change of kubelet CRI package

Issue description:
We have moved CRI from [api/v1alpha1/runtime](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/kubelet/api/v1alpha1/runtime) to [apis/cri/v1alpha1](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/kubelet/apis/cri/v1alpha1), which changed the package name of CRI. - **Kernel** (e.g. `uname -a`): 4.9.24
- **Install tools**: Custom AMI


**What happened**:
The service controller deletes and re-adds the ELB listeners when it starts up (or becomes the master).

**What you expected to happen**:
It should only modify the listeners if they have actually changed.

**How to reproduce it** (as minimally and precisely as possible):
- Create a service with type `LoadBalancer`
- Restart controller-manager after ELB has been created
- Search CloudTrail for events for the ELB, and verify there are DeleteLoadBalancerListeners and CreateLoadBalancerListeners events.

**Anything else we need to know**:

I believe this is caused by [this for loop](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cc568f6433f2d90b30ca8e1d51f3597d60affb11/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/aws/aws_loadbalancer.go#L192-L209) in the `ensureLoadBalancer` function which compares the desired listener properties to the actual listener properties.

The problem is that K8 uses lowercase strings [1](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cc568f6433f2d90b30ca8e1d51f3597d60affb11/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/aws/aws.go#L2554), [2](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cc568f6433f2d90b30ca8e1d51f3597d60affb11/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/aws/aws_test.go#L1149) for the protocols, but AWS returns uppercase protocols when describing the listeners (see the two example outputs below).

I believe the simplest fix is to lowercase the protocols in the for loop when performing the comparison, which I can submit as a PR if others agree with that solution.

```
$ aws elb describe-load-balancers --load-balancer-names a4fafa3e6f24911e6aac506402a2bc46

                        "LoadBalancerPort": 80,

                        "InstanceProtocol": "TCP"
                    },
                    "PolicyNames": []
                }
            ]
        }
    ]
}
```

```

import (
	"log"

	"github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/aws/session"
	"github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/service/elb"
)

func main() {
	name := "a4fafa3e6f24911e6aac506402a2bc46"

	sess := session.Must(session.NewSession())
	svc := elb.New(sess)

	request := &elb.DescribeLoadBalancersInput{}
	request.LoadBalancerNames = []*string{&name}

	response, err := svc.DescribeLoadBalancers(request)
	if err != nil {

	}

	for _, loadBalancer := range response.LoadBalancerDescriptions {

		return
	}
}

Issue #47092: [GCE] Shared backend services for ILBs leak settings to other ILBs

Issue description:
PR #46663 GCP internal load balancers for services with type LoadBalancer and an annotation specifying "internal".  If the load balancer has `externalTrafficPolicy=Global`, we generate a backend service name such as `k8s-{clusterid}-internal-[tcp/udp]-[clientip|noaffinity]`. This allows other ILBs to utilize the same backend service to keep stay below quota.

However, there are more service settings like `TimeoutSec` and `IAP` which could be unique to a single or multiple load balancers. **Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**: Feature

Default FlexVolume driver directory is `/usr/libexec/kubernetes/kubelet-plugins/volume/exec/`, which is not writable on COS images. Should have a different default directory to enable FlexVolume on COS.

/kind feature

/assign @verult

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Setting default FlexVolume driver directory on COS images.
PR description:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:
1. If this is your first time, read our contributor guidelines https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/pull-requests.md#the-pr-submit-process and developer guide https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/development.md#development-guide

3. Follow the instructions for writing a release note: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/pull-requests.md#write-release-notes-if-needed
-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**: The original default FlexVolume driver directory is not writable on COS. A new location is necessary to make FlexVolume work.

**What happened**:
When creating a RBD StorageClass without explicitly setting the `adminId` parameter and later removing a PVC, the corresponding PV goes into failed state.
Relevant logs are:
```
{"log":"E0715 08:16:20.765812       1 rbd_util.go:402] failed to delete rbd image: exit status 1, command output: 2017-07-15 08:16:20.660590 7f77606bc780 -1 did not load config file, using default settings.\n","stream":"stderr","time":"2017-07-15T08:16:20.766155923Z"}

{"log":"rbd: couldn't connect to the cluster!\n","stream":"stderr","time":"2017-07-15T08:16:20.766182457Z"}
```

After looking at the code, I see that default value for `adminId` (which is "admin" as is stated in the [documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes/#ceph-rbd)) is only [checked when provisioning a volume](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.7/pkg/volume/rbd/rbd.go#L308). However when deleting a volume, [there is no check](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.7/pkg/volume/rbd/rbd.go#L202). The value is empty, that explains the `client.` part of the log, usually this is `client.admin`

The volume to get released and deleted.

/kind bug

`.git` is ignored as before, unless it's needed by the current script. In case `.git` is about to be `rsync`ed, a warning needs to be printed.

Just run `build/run.sh`. Doing so against a remote docker over slow(ish) Internet connection will make the behavior apparent.

For now perhaps only `update-staging-godeps` script needs to rsync `.git` IIUC (see #46193).

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #49308: Extend cloudprovider Zones API to support out-of-tree CCMs

Issue description:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

/kind bug

**What happened**:

I'm currently part of a team working on implementing an out-of-tree cloud controller manager (CCM) for [Oracle Bare Metal Cloud][4].

For in-tree cloud-providers the [`cloudprovider.GetZone()`][1] method is [called from `kubelet`][2]. This allows in-tree cloud providers to implement [`GetZone()`][1] by querying local metadata services (as `kubelet` is of course running on the node itself).

For out-of-tree cloud-providers [`GetZone()`][1] is called in [`AddCloudNode()`][3] in the context of the cloud-controller-manager binary. Thus, local metadata services return the failure zone and region for the node on which the CCM is running rather than the node itself.

**What you expected to happen**:

Out-of-tree cloud providers should have access to the same functionality as in-tree cloud-providers.

I propose extending the [`cloudprovider.Zones()`][5] interface to include a `GetZoneByProviderID(providerId string)` method and utilising this method in [`AddCloudNode()`][3].

Alternatively (or additionally) the signature of [`GetZone()`][1] could be modified to take a `types.NodeName` parameter and the existing cloud-providers updated. This would be consistent with the other interfaces in the `cloudprovider` package.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

 - Deploy an out-of-tree cloud controller manager as a daemon set running on the master nodes.
 - Add node to cluster in a different failure zone to the node on which the leader CCM is running.
 - Note that the node is labeled as being in the failure zone and region of the node the CCM is running on.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

I am very happy to implement this as an initial contribution to k8s if there is consensus on the issue.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
   ```
   Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"7", GitVersion:"v1.7.1", GitCommit:"1dc5c66f5dd61da08412a74221ecc79208c2165b", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2017-07-14T02:00:46Z", GoVersion:"go1.8.3", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
   Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"7", GitVersion:"v1.7.0", GitCommit:"d3ada0119e776222f11ec7945e6d860061339aad", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2017-06-29T22:55:19Z", GoVersion:"go1.8.3", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
   ```

- Install tools: `kubeadm`

/cc @luxas @thockin @wlan0 @rrati @roberthbailey @tjfontaine

Issue #51319: "NoNewPrivs" is admitted only if the runtime is docker or rkt in kubelet

Issue description:
I tried to add the `NoNewPrivs` support for `cri-containerd`, but the `test-e2e-node` always failed with the error print:
```
E0825 13:03:23.824134     814 pod_workers.go:182] Error syncing pod 29b8ba92-8952-11e7-93c7-5254003d4460 ("alpine-nnp-false-29ab6dfa-8952-11e7-958f-5254003d4460_e2e-tests-security-context-test-4jdbq(29b8ba92-8952-11e7-93c7-5254003d4460)"), skipping: pod cannot be run: Cannot enforce NoNewPrivs: containerd runtime not supported
```

I checked the code of k8s, and found that "NoNewPrivs" is admitted only if the runtime is docker or rkt in kubelet. Related code is as follows:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0cf928f6813741d9699786ee61ec014c90119e2c/pkg/kubelet/lifecycle/handlers.go#L190-L225

Maybe we should define a interface to get the capability of "NoNewPrivs" form runtime-shim.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #51842: Quota replenishment controller doesn't handle uninitialized objects

Issue description:
The quota is charged when an object is created, no matter if it's initialized or not. It has two problems:

* The quota replenish controller doesn't list/watch uninitialized objects, so it misses the deletion of uninitialized objects and leaks quota.

* The quota controller does periodic resync to recalculate the quota usage. It doesn't see the uninitialized objects, and will wrongly replenish the quota for yet-to-initialize objects.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/51749 makes most quota to be charged after the objects are initialized. But the object count quota is still (and ought to be) charged when an object is created, so it still suffers the above problems.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Charges quota only for initialized objects
PR description:
Partially fix https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/51842.

Based on https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/51733/files. Only the commit "Don't charge quota when creating/updating an uninitialized object" is new.

The old plan was to charge quota for each update of uninitialized object. This PR makes the quota admission only charges the update that removes the last pending initializer. Because
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/51247, which lets sharedInformer see uninitialized objects, is not making the code freeze deadline. Hence, the quota replenishing controller won't capture deletion of uninitialized objects. We will leak quota if we charge quota for uninitialized objects.
* @lavalamp @erictune pointed out calculating/reserving quota is expensive, we should avoid doing it for every initializer update.
* My original argument was that quota admission should fail early so that user can easily figure out which initializer causes the quota outage. @lavalamp @erictune convinced me that user could easily figure the culprit if they watch the initialization process.

The only exception is the object count quota, which is charged whenever the object is created. This is to prevent attack from bypassing the object count quota to create too many uninitialized objects.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #52830: Not working if gophercloud Identity Versionless Endpoint

Issue description:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:
/kind bug
/sig openstack


**What happened**:
Currently the auth-url of openstack cloud provider must contains keystone version(v2 or v3), or it can't init openstack client.
However, I started digging into this and I found that Keystone is now replying with version v3.8 instead of v3.0, so we need support 3.0 and 3.8.
It is really easy to test since now devstack provides Keystone on /identity

**What you expected to happen**:
Support handling New Identity Endpoints: Identity Versionless Endpoint

1. Identity endpoints published with a valid URL path
(http://example.com/identity) are now parsed correctly.

If the endpoint has a version suffix (http://example.com/identity/v3),
the client will use /identity as the base and /identity/v3 as the
endpoint.

If the endpoint does not have a version suffix, both the base and the
endpoint will be set to /identity and further version discovery will
be done.

2. Version discovery can now handle version IDs other than v2.0 and v3.
If the Identity Service is publishing an ID of v3.8, Gophercloud will
recognize it as a valid result.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #52988: Cpu Manager e2e node tests fail

Issue description:
/kind bug

**What happened**:
Cpu manager node e2e tests fail due to mismatch in cpu assignment.

```
Sep 25 13:45:45.340: INFO: Unexpected error occurred: failed to match regexp "^1\n$" in output "4\n"
```

Followed by
```
 expected log not found in container [gu-container] of pod [gu-pod]
    Expected error:
        <*errors.errorString | 0xc4203e9b90>: {
            s: "failed to match regexp \"^1\\n$\" in output \"4\\n\"",
        }
        failed to match regexp "^1\n$" in output "4\n"
    not to have occurred

```

This is caused by not detecting whether HT is enabled on platform properly.
`isHTEnabled()` does `lscpu | grep \"Thread(s) per core:\" | cut -c24` whereas on some systems
`-c22` is needed.
`lscpu` output line char should not be hard-coded.


**What you expected to happen**:
Expect tests to pass.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Run `make test-e2e-node TEST_ARGS='--feature-gates=DynamicKubeletConfig=true' FOCUS="CPU Manager" SKIP="" PARALLELISM=1` on Fedora26

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #53554: IPv6 IPs derived incorrectly in proxier's deleteEndpointConnections

Issue description:
<!-- This form is for bug reports and feature requests ONLY!

If you're looking for help check [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/kubernetes) and the [troubleshooting guide](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug-application-cluster/troubleshooting/).
-->

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

> Uncomment only one, leave it on its own line:
>
> /kind bug
/kind feature

/sig network
/area ipv6

**What happened**:
The calculation of endpointIP in the iptables proxier's deleteEndpointConnections() method does not handle endpoints of the form [ipv6-address]:port. The current logic strips off anything after the first colon it finds:
```
endpointIP := epSvcPair.endpoint[0:strings.Index(epSvcPair.endpoint, ":")]
```
so this won't work for IPv6. This can be seen on code inspection. It can also cause problems when running e2e networking tests that include UDP connections, whereby the kube-proxy will crash on a conntrack command, and restart.

**What you expected to happen**:
The code needs to derive IPv6 addresses from IPv6 endpoints of the form "[IPv6]:port", as well as deriving IPv4 addresses from IPv4 endpoints of the form "IPv4:port".

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Code inspection, or run e2e UDP networking tests on an IPv6-only cluster (and watch for kube-proxy restarts).

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): Latest master
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration**: VirtualBox cluster, Ubuntu 16.04.1 host, CentOS 7 guests
- OS (e.g. from /etc/os-release): CentOS 7
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 3.10.0-514.26.2.el7.x86_64 #1 SMP Tue Jul 4 15:04:05 UTC 2017 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
- Install tools:
- Others:

PR title: Add IPv6 and negative UT test cases for proxier's deleteEndpointConnections
PR description:
This change adds IPv6 and negative UT test cases for the proxier's deleteEndpointConnections.

Changes include:
- Add IPv6 UT test cases to TestDeleteEndpointConnections.
- Add negative UT test case to TestDeleteEndpointConnections for
  handling case where no connections need clearing (benign error).
- Add negative UT test case to test unexpected error.
- Reorganize UT in TestDeleteEndpointConnections so that the fake
  command executor's command and scripted responses are generated on
  the fly based on the test case table (rather than using a fixed
  set of commands/responses that will need to be updated every time
  test cases are added/deleted).
- Create the proxier service map in real time, based on the test case
  table (rather than using a fixed service map that will need to be updated
  every time test cases are added/deleted).

fixes #53554

Looking at a heap profile showed, that the majority of this memory is coming from the [`cache.NewNamedReflector`](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/82aa063804cf055e16e8911250f888bc216e8b61/tools/cache/reflector.go#L107) function, or more specifically, the [metrics being instantiated in it](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/82aa063804cf055e16e8911250f888bc216e8b61/tools/cache/reflector.go#L112).

[pprof.hyperkube.alloc_objects.alloc_space.inuse_objects.inuse_space.003.pb.gz](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/files/1358504/pprof.hyperkube.alloc_objects.alloc_space.inuse_objects.inuse_space.003.pb.gz)

I validated that this is indeed coming from metrics by checking the amount of metrics exposed by the `/metrics` endpoint.

```
$ curl localhost:8001/metrics | wc -l
49966
```

In an equivalent workload cluster running Kubernetes `v1.7.5`, this number is round `3000`.

So I took a look and noticed, that the majority of these metrics are actually coming from reflectors of CRD resources. Around 15000 of those metrics are each related to one of the three CRDs installed in the cluster. The total number of metrics increases by ~50 every few minutes.

I feel this might be happening whenever the cache in the Prometheus Operator (the controller for the CRDs existing in this cluster) is hitting its resync interval for a particular resource, so this might be happening on either opening a watch and or listing the resources, but this is just a wild guess.

The metrics in the `NewNamedReflector` function should be injected instead of re-created and registered on the global metrics registry, but the fact that the apiserver keeps creating new reflectors for these resources is likely also a problem.

Another problem I've been noticing, starting approximately at the same time as this, is that the apiserver API latencies have increased significantly.

**What you expected to happen**:

Unique metrics for each type of reflector, not causing a memory leak.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

The cluster was setup using bootkube, but recently upgraded to 1.8 (3 days ago), and the Prometheus Operator running on it with the [`kube-prometheus`](https://github.com/coreos/prometheus-operator/tree/master/contrib/kube-prometheus) stack deployed.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**: bootkube / bare metal
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.8
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration**:
- OS (e.g. from /etc/os-release): CoreOS Container Linux
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): Linux sd-99796 4.12.14-coreos #1 SMP Wed Sep 20 22:20:05 UTC 2017 x86_64
- Install tools: bootkube
- Others:

@sig-instrumentation-bugs @kubernetes/sig-api-machinery-bugs

/cc @sttts @nikhita I know you recently worked on the CRD code, so you may know why there are new reflectors being created constantly.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #53757: CRI: Debug API

Issue description:
Today, CRI only provides information needed by Kubelet.

But actually, Kubelet is not the only consumer of CRI. [`crilctl`](https://github.com/kubernetes-incubator/cri-tools/blob/master/docs/crictl.md), which is a CLI tool for debugging purpose, also talks with CRI to get debug information for user.

Most operations provided in `crictl` are well covered by CRI already. The only thing missing is detailed debug information about `container`, `sandbox`, `image` and `container runtime` itself (think about `docker inspect` and `docker info`). For linux container based container runtime, it could be `Pid`, `Namespaces`, `Container Config` etc.

Since we want `crictl` to be portable across different CRI container runtimes, it has to get the debug information from CRI instead of from the underlying container runtime directly.

Ideally,
- Each container runtime should be able to provide runtime specific debug information via CRI.
- Kubelet should never consume that information.
- `crictl` should easily format and print the debug information to user.

**The debug information could just be a string in `json` format**, which could be easily combined, converted and printed.

As for how to expose the debug information through CRI, there are several options:
- **Option 1:** Add a `ContainerInfo` field in `ContainerStatusResponse`, and also corresponding fields in `PodSandboxStatusResponse`, `ImageStatusResponse` and `StatusResponse`. The `ContainerInfo` is just a string in json format.
  - Pros: Won't break existing CRI container runtime. If they don't want to provide this, they could just return empty.
  - Cons: This introduces extra overhead in each status call, the extra encoding/decoding in grpc will be a pain. And the more debug information a container runtime provides, the worse its performance is, which doesn't seem like an encouragement to more debug info.
- **Option 2 (Preferred):** Same with Option 1, but add a `Debug bool` option in `ContainerStatusRequest`, and also other status requests. Container runtime should only provide extra debug information when `Debug=true`.
  - Pros: Extra debug information doesn't add extra performance overhead in production.
  - Cons: The `Debug` option may be confusing to people, we may need another name.
- **Option 3:** Add separate CRI functions for the debug information.
  - Pros: More clear.
  - Cons: All CRI runtimes need to support these functions, at least need to return `not implemented` for those functions.
- **Option 4:** Separate CRI debug API. `crictl` should only use it when it is present, and just use CRI if it isn't.
  - Pros: Clean. The original CRI won't be affected at all.
  - Cons: More complex than option 2.

I personally prefer option 2, but am open to other options. :)

Issue #53906: cannot apply networking.k8s.io/v1 - updates to networkpolicy spec are forbidden

Issue description:
Hi all,

/sig area/kubectl
/sig sig/network
@kubernetes/sig-network-bugs

We made the upstep from k8s 1.6 to 1.7.8 on our k8s clusters. As good k8s citizens, we have updated our NetworkPolicy yaml deployment files to use the new **networking.k8s.io/v1** apiVersion. It appears however that a retrieval of NetworkPolicies deployed this way, still use the **extensions/v1beta1** apiVersion. I suppose this is due to backwards compatibility concerns, which I can perfectly understand.

What is the issue however, is that we deploy our NetworkPolicies (in an automated way, using a cluster applier process within each namespace, that pulls the yaml config from git and applies them periodically) using "kubectl apply -f *.yaml". The kubectl client however refuses to do so, since he detects a _false_ change between what's deployed (extensions/v1beta1) and what's to be deployed (networking.k8s.io/v1). I'd expect the same compatibility check/measures at apply time (not only at fetch/retrieval time).

Does anyone have any advice on how to get around this? We know that we could write a more advanced cluster applier process that circumvents this corner cases in an if-then-else matter, but I would expect the kubectl client to handle those things, or am I overlooking a certain kubectl feature here?

Best regards,
Bart

PR title: Fix Incorrect Scale Subresources and HPA e2e ScaleTargetRefs
PR description:
The HPA e2es failed to actually set `apiVersion` on the created HPAs, which previous was ignored.  Since the polymorphic scale client was merged, this behavior is no longer tolerated (it was never correct to begin with, but it accidentally worked).

Additionally, the `apps` resources have their own version of scale.  Until `apps/v1beta1` and `apps/v1beta2` go away, we need to support those versions in the scale client.

Together, these broke some of the HPA e2es.

Fixes #54574

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #55553: Zero capacity PVs cause pods to fail and zero capacity PVCs create zero capacity PVs

Issue description:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**: BUG REPORT

/kind bug

**What happened**: If someone requests a zero (0) capacity PVC and an administrator creates a zero (0) capacity PV, Kubernetes will happily bind them together. Unfortunately, any use of this PVC/PV combination by a pod will fail. It fails because the zero capacity PV cannot be formatted or mounted successfully.

Note: The same issue happens for dynamically provisioned PVs.

**What you expected to happen**: I expect that Kubernetes would not allow creation of invalid PVC and PV objects, aka zero (0) capacity PVs and PVCs.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**: Create a pod that requests a zero capacity PVC, using dynamic PV provisioning is simpler than creating your own zero (0) capacity PV. The pod will fail to reach a running state, since the related PV fails to be formatted and mounted successfully.

Here is the error that I received for a test I performed requesting a zero capacity PVC using ceph rbd:
```

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #55620: kubelet: corrupt dockershim checkpoint jams up CNI

Issue description:
There is currently a bug with the docker shim checkpoint file when the file is corrupt that can cause the kubelet to not be able to stop a sandbox.

The issue occurs because `buildCNIRuntimeConf()` modifies the error from `GetPodPortMappings()` as it propagates the error:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/network/cni/cni.go#L303

The corrupted checkpoint file should be removed by the higher level:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/dockershim/docker_sandbox.go#L200

But because the error has been modified, this is not run and treated as an unhandled error, continuously blocking `StopPodSandbox()`.

Results in continuous `could not retrieve port mappings: checkpoint is corrupted` errors.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: dockershim: remove corrupt checkpoints immediately upon detection
PR description:
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/55620

The current checkpoint abstraction leaks the handling of corrupt checkpoints to the user.

If the user does a `GetCheckpoint()` and the checkpoint is corrupt, the corrupt checkpoint is returned to the user (why??) with an error indicating the corruption.  It is then up to the user to detect the corruption via the error msg and call `RemoveCheckpoint()` to remove the corrupted checkpoint.

The checkpoint abstraction should not expose corruption to the user.  If it is corrupt, it is as good as not found to the user.  The checkpoint code should handle cleanup of corrupt entries and report "not found" to the user.

Issue description:
We should allow to pass a tcp listener into an API server via GenericApiServer config. This will allow us to use kernel zero-port allocation `localhost:0` to find a free port instead of the retry loops we have everywhere in tests.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #55007: kubelet starts too many `udevadm trigger`

Issue description:
/kind bug

**What happened**:
kubelet creates too many udev "change" events during Cinder volume attachment.
If volume attachement takes long, then udev event queue gets full, therefore
udev does not answer requests from docker, and PLEG makes the k8s node unhealthy.

**What you expected to happen**:
  * kubelet should not run `udevadm trigger` so often.
  * kubelet should run `udevadm settle --timeout=1 && udevadm trigger`

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Deploy k8s on Openstack. Configure k8s cluster with --cloud_provider=openstack.
  * Cordon all nodes except one.
  * SSH into that node. Start `udevadm monitor` and let it run.
  * Create StorateClass for Cinder volumes.
  * Deploy StatefulSet with volumeClaimTemplate pointing to that StorageClass.
  * Optionally, immediately detatch the newly-created cinder volume manually
    through openstack CLI or web interface to simulate a slow cinder attachment.
  * Look back to the `udevadm monitor` to find thousands of udev events.
    In case of the "show" attachement, the "change" udev events will never stop.
  * Also run `top` to find that systemd-udevd consumes 100% CPU.
  * Also run `docker ps` to find that it hangs and never answers.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
Attachment of a new cinder volume includes execution of `udevadm trigger`
command, see links (1-3) below. The `udevadm trigger` generates a "change"
event for every single device on the /sys/devices SysFS. This can be seen by
running `udevadm monitor`.

The execution stack is as follows:
  * Volume Attacher Interface (1) runs WaitForAttach(), which is implemented in (2).
  * The Cinder's WaitForAttach() runs probeAttachedVolume() 2 times per second
    (lines 243 and 247). The "1 second" retry timeout is defined by (3).
  * The probeAttachedVolume() is defined in (4). It triggers SCSI rescan and
    generates udev "change" event on all devices by running `udevadm trigger`.

As you see, both scsi rescan and full udev rescan are triggered 2 times per second.

The scsi bus rescan leads to considerable latency of runnig I/O operations.

The sysemd-udevd is unable to process so many "change" events. The udev queue
gets full, leading to frozen `docker ps` operation that cAdvisor runs every 2 seconds.
After 3 minutes, kubelet marks itself unhealthy (5) due to PLEG (6).


(1) [Volume Attacher interface runs WaitForAttach()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2723e06a251a4ec3ef241397217e73fa782b0b98/pkg/volume/volume.go#L176)
(2) [Cinder Attacher implementation of WaitForAttach()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2723e06a251a4ec3ef241397217e73fa782b0b98/pkg/volume/cinder/attacher.go#L224)
(3) [1 second retry timeout](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2723e06a251a4ec3ef241397217e73fa782b0b98/pkg/volume/cinder/attacher.go#L237)
(4) [probeAttachedVolume()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fc8bfe2d8929e11a898c4557f9323c482b5e8842/pkg/volume/cinder/cinder_util.go#L222)
(5) [PLEG healthcheck](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/eb658d699ac074ef2a6f3808b13aacc6adfca786/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L748)
(6) [PLEG implementation](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d196a4abbbf3f1ca458908abd42267b521a6faff/pkg/kubelet/pleg/generic.go#L133)

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #56234: [Test Failure] Disk metrics appear to be off on coreos

Issue description:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:
Bug Report
/kind bug

**What happened**:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/54316 improved disk eviction testing to make it more precise.  For example, it expects a pod which uses 299 Mb of disk not to be evicted if it sets its limit to 300 Mi.  As shown on [the testgrid](https://k8s-testgrid.appspot.com/sig-node-kubelet#kubelet-flaky-gce-e2e&include-filter-by-regex=PriorityLocalStorage), this test passes for all OS distributions except CoreOS.  I have ruled out an issue with the storage driver and backing filesystem since both COS and CoreOS use overlay backed by extfs.

**What you expected to happen**:
I expected the pod using 299Mb not to be evicted when its limit is 300 Mb.
I expected not to see this event:
`reason: 'Evicted' pod ephemeral local storage usage exceeds the total limit of containers {{314572800 0} {<nil>} 300Mi BinarySI}`

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
The container runs this command to use 299Mb:
`i=0; while [ $i -lt 299 ]; do dd if=/dev/urandom of=%s${i} bs=1048576 count=1; i=$(($i+1)); done; while true; do sleep 5; done`
Each iteration writes 1Mb to disk, producing a total of 299 Mb of disk usage.
The pod has `limits` set to 300Mi.
The test has the LocalStorageCapacityIsolation feature gate enabled.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
This may be a discrepancy in the `du` (which we use to measure container disk usage) or `dd`, which is used by the test to write exact quantities of disk.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: e2e: eviction test redirect dd stderr

Issue #56730: Back-port scheduler cache panic fix to 1.8 and 1.7

Issue description:
<!-- This form is for bug reports and feature requests ONLY!

If you're looking for help check [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/kubernetes) and the [troubleshooting guide](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug-application-cluster/troubleshooting/).

There was a bug in scheduler which is fixed in 1.9 and later as a part of [this PR](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/55039). We need to backport it to 1.8 and 1.7.

The sequence of events to trigger this issue is:
 - Pod fails predicates, pod condition was updated with the predicate error.
 - Pod passes predicates
 - Pod fails bind, pod condition was updated with the bind error.

The Conditions in assumedPod is the same ptr as in pod because [assumedPod is a shallow copy](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.8/plugin/pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go#L320), not a DeepCopy of pod.
Changing the assumedPod condition causes a cache panic.

Issue #57277: invalid manifest for CoreDNS logging when started with kubeadm

Issue description:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**: BUG
> /kind bug

**What happened**:

When CoreDNS is deployed by default using feature-gates of kubeadm, it does not log anything when processing a DNS query.

That is due to change of log option of CoreDNS in latest version.
that version was bumped up in kubeadm, but the manifest was not adapted to the new log option.

- initial change of 'log stdout' in CoreDNS : https://github.com/coredns/coredns/issues/1218
- version of CoreDNS 1.0.0 bumped into Kubeadm : #56802

NOTE: I guess we should also changed manifests for kube-up : see #55728


The change in manifest expected is to remove the option "stdout" in the line "log ...". As it is now interpreted as a scope of domain to log.

Invalid manifest:
>   Corefile: |
>      .:53 {
>           errors
>           **log stdout**
>           health
>         ....
>

Correct manifest:
>    Corefile: |
>      .:53 {
>           errors
>           **log**
>           health
>         ....


**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.9 and MAIN
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: any
- Install tools: kubeadm, kube-up

## Workaround for installation that needs the log

1. update the configmap for coredns

`kubectl get configmaps -n kube-system coredns -o yaml | sed "s/log stdout/log/g" | kubectl replace -f -
`

2. restart the coredns deployment

`
kubectl scale deployment --replicas=0 -n kube-system coredns
`
`
kubectl scale deployment --replicas=1 -n kube-system coredns
`

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #21305: iscsi: set node.startup to manual

Issue description:
I'm not sure if this is desired behaviour or not but currently if the following scenario happens
1. iscsid.conf has node.startup set to automatic (default value)
2. kubelet is running a pod with a mapped iscsi volume
3. The node reboots/crashes etc
4. Kubescheduler reschedules the pod to another node
5. The node comes up again and will try to re open the session to the target that the pod was using. This can either cause annoyance or worst case data corruption unless the iscsi target is set to reject more than one session per target

If we instead set the following when login into the target the session won't be reopened
iscsiadm -m node --targetname proper_target_name -p target_IP:port -o update -n node.startup -v manual

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: iscsi: set node.startup to manual
PR description:
If the default iSCSI node.startup is set to automatic, if there is a node failure,
any pods on that node will get rescheduled to another node. If the failed node is
later brought back up it will then try to log back in to any iSCSI sessions it had
prior to the failure, which may no longer exist or may be now in-use by the other
nodes.

It appears most platforms keep the open-iscsi default of node.startup-automatic.
But in case this system-wide setting has been changed, and just to be explicit, this
sets node.startup values for kubernetes controlled volumes to manual.

Fixes #21305

```release-note
iSCSI sessions managed by kubernetes will now explicitly set startup.mode to 'manual' to
prevent automatic login after node failure recovery. This is the default open-iscsi mode, so
this change will only impact users who have changed their startup.mode to be 'automatic'
in /etc/iscsi/iscsid.conf.
```
