A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #93106: Azure cloud provider hits the VMSS VMs List API more than it should

Issue description:
**What happened**:

Running a non-AKS k8s v1.18.5  cluster on Azure, with 50 VMSS attached (each containing one or two nodes).

When we do attach several new VMSSes, or create/replace several nodes, the controller-managed gets quickly throttled by Azure API, for instance like so:
```
kube-controller-manager[2014310]: E0708 08:33:13.752989 2014310 azure_vmss.go:570]
VirtualMachineScaleSetsClient.List failed:
&{true 0 2020-07-08 08:34:43.665286837 +0000 UTC m=+1598.271278798
azure cloud provider throttled for operation VMSSList with reason "client throttled"}
```

Having a closer look at the cloud provider code, we see controller-manager would re-scan all attached VMSS on cache miss or expired TTL. Not just the one that needs a refresh.

**What you expected to happen**:

Number of VMSS List calls should be linear (eg. one for a new instance's showing up or being deleted), and not O(number of vmss).

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Attach many VMSS (even if they contain a single VM) to a cluster, then attach more or create many pods with remote PVs.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.18.5
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: Azure
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Ubuntu 20.04
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 5.4.0
- Controller-manager cloud-config:
```
{
  "subscriptionId": "xxx",
  "resourceGroup": "yyy",
  "location": "westus2",
  "vnetName": "www",
  "vnetResourceGroup": "zzz",
  "vmType": "vmss",
  "loadBalancerSku": "standard",
  "useManagedIdentityExtension": true,
  "excludeMasterFromStandardLB": true,
  "useInstanceMetadata": true,
  "cloudConfigType": "file",
  "vmssCacheTTLInSeconds": 900,
  "vmssVirtualMachinesCacheTTLInSeconds": 900,
  "vmCacheTTLInSeconds": 900
}
```

PR title: Azure: use per-vmss vmssvm incremental cache
PR description:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Azure's cloud provider VMSS VMs API accesses are mediated through a cache holding and refreshing all VMSS together.

Due to that we hit VMSSVM.List API more often than we could: an instance's cache miss or expiration should only require a single VMSS re-list, while it's currently O(n) relative to the number of attached Scale Sets.

Under hard pressure (clusters with many attached VMSS that can't all be listed in one sequence of successive API calls) the controller manager might be stuck trying to re-list everything from scratch, then aborting the whole operation due to rate limits, affecting the whole Subscription.

This patch replaces the global VMSS VMs cache by per-VMSS VMs caches.  Refreshes (VMSS VMs lists) are scoped to the single relevant VMSS; under severe throttling the various caches can be incrementally refreshed.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #93106

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

We are assuming VMSS nodes are named from VMSS' computerNamePrefix+id (or vmssName+id, when computerNamePrefix isn't specified), as described [https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machine-scale-sets/virtual-machine-scale-sets-instance-ids](here) and [https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.compute/2018-10-01/virtualmachinescalesets#virtualmachinescalesetosprofile-object](there). Are there special cases not covered by that doc? if so we can probably complement that optimistic lookup (trying the vmss matching name prefix first, happy path) by a fallback to a scan over remaining scale sets. The non-optimal fallback path would still be an improvement as (in case of throttling) we keep partial results (per VMSS caches), refreshes are incremental.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
Azure: per VMSS VMSS VMs cache to prevent throttling on clusters having many attached VMSS
```

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

When a node is deleted and then recreated in short time, the "instance not found" error would be reported from Azure cloud provider and hence the node object is deleted by kube-controller-manager.

It is because the deleted VMSS VM would be cached for 15 minutes (this is used to avoid throttling issues when a large number of nodes are deleted) and the cache TTL is not configurable.

This PR fixes the issue by

1) Refresh the cache if the deleted VM has been cached for VmssVirtualMachinesCacheTTLInSeconds period.
2) letting the cache TTL configurable via VmssVirtualMachinesCacheTTLInSeconds.

**What happened**:
Testing API Priority and Fairness, I issued this command in a rather idle cluster:
```shell
kubectl get --raw '/debug/api_priority_and_fairness/dump_requests?includeRequestDetails=1'
```
and I got this result:
```
PriorityLevelName, FlowSchemaName, QueueIndex, RequestIndexInQueue, FlowDistingsher, ArriveTime, UserName, Verb,   APIPath, Namespace, Name,   APIVersion, Resource, SubResource,
exempt,            <none>,         <none>,     <none>,              <none>,          <none>,     <none>,   <none>, <none>,  <none>,    <none>, <none>,     <none>,   <none>,
```

That is, a list of one request with no information of any sort.  That comes from https://github.com/kubernetes/apiserver/blob/24947093e02e913416119fa204aa61fb7da6533b/pkg/util/flowcontrol/apf_controller_debug.go#L165-L188 , which invents one phantom request for each priority level that is exempt.  We do not want or need a phantom request; `dump_requests` is for listing requests in queues.

I expected to get only queued requests.

/kind bug

> /kind cleanup
> /kind deprecation
> /kind design
> /kind documentation
> /kind failing-test
> /kind feature

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
When a service is deleted or updated, the service becomes stale and is cleaned up. In the current logic this service cleanup can be triggered multiple times. Except the first cleanup the subsequent cleanup calls are a no-op. But as part of service cleanup the endpoints in the endpoint map are attempted to be cleaned up a second time and dereferenced twice.

In a scenario where the remote endpoints are shared across two services, the second dereference causes the remote endpoint to be deleted from HNS. This breaks connectivity to the service.

**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
The Job controller currently uses `NumRequeues` to decide wether or not the job has exceeded the backoffLimit. `NumRequeues` represents the number of times a job has been requeued, a requeue can occur due to several reasons and not only for Fail events. This makes backoffLimit unpredictable.

This PR sets the job controller to use the number of `Failed` pods to decide if the job has exceeded the backoffLimit.

According to the documentation: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/design-proposals/apps/job.md#backoff-policy-and-failed-pod-limit

> For Never we count actual pod failures (reflected in .status.failed field). With OnFailure, we take an approximate value of pod restarts (as reported in .status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount).

For restart policy of `OnFailure` - the logic is handled in `pastBackoffLimitOnFailure` as described above.
For restart policy of `Never` - this PR fixes the logic to be as described above.

This solution has been discussed in the past by @janetkuo  in: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/70251#issuecomment-433507671

PR title: test(endpoints): deflake TestWatchHTTPTimeout
PR description:
Signed-off-by: knight42 <anonymousknight96@gmail.com>


**What type of PR is this?**

/kind flake

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

I added the following logging
```diff
diff --git staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/watch/watch.go staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/watch/watch.go
index 1f4911a3113..3ea8049dcbb 100644
--- staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/watch/watch.go
+++ staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/watch/watch.go
@@ -112,6 +112,7 @@ func NewFakeWithChanSize(size int, blocking bool) *FakeWatcher {
 func (f *FakeWatcher) Stop() {
        f.Lock()
        defer f.Unlock()
+       fmt.Println("Stop called")
        if !f.stopped {
                klog.V(4).Infof("Stopping fake watcher.")
                close(f.result)
@@ -122,6 +123,7 @@ func (f *FakeWatcher) Stop() {
 func (f *FakeWatcher) IsStopped() bool {
        f.Lock()
        defer f.Unlock()
+       fmt.Println("IsStopped called")
        return f.stopped
 }
```
and notice when the test fails, `FakeWatcher.IsStopped` is invoked before `FakeWatcher.Stop`:
```
...
Stop called
IsStopped called
PASS
Stop called
IsStopped called
PASS
IsStopped called
Stop called
--- FAIL: TestWatchHTTPTimeout (0.00s)
    watch_test.go:848: Leaked watch on timeout
FAIL
```

----

To understand what is happening, we need to know there are two goroutines here:

```go
// simplified goroutine A: request handler
func(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
    defer watcher.Stop()

    watchServer.ServeHTTP(w, req)
}
```

```go
// simplified goroutine B: ServeHTTP
func (s *WatchServer) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
    defer close(done)

    select {
    case <-timeoutCh:
        return
    }
}
```

When we `close(timeoutCh)` at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/watch_test.go#L844, goroutine B `close(done)` and returns, but `watcher.Stop` would only be called just before goroutine A returns. It is not guranteed that `watcher.Stop` has been invoked when we call `watcher.IsStopped` at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/04362870ad9f9812f487ab8f89a40f6bf2daa588/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/watch_test.go#L845-L849.

As a result, instead of invoking `watcher.IsStopped` I decide to check if `watcher.ResultChan()` is closed, which seems to be more robust.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #63906: Autogenerated container port name conflicts with multiple hostports

Issue description:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

/kind bug

**What happened**:

A container ports spec such as:
```
        ports:
        - containerPort: 4443
          hostPort: 443
        - containerPort: 4443
          hostPort: 4443
```
Results in this error:
```
kubelet[11270]: W0515 17:44:41.623947   11270 helpers.go:352] Port name conflicted, "cntr-TCP:4443" is defined more than once

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #90652: Reduce the number of calls to GCE API (for clusters on GCE) coming from cloud node-controller

Issue description:
For external cloud provider - Kubelet setting the TaintExternalCloudProvider taint: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_node_status.go#L266

The results in calling `initializeNode` function in cloud node-controller:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c276a451d64d161b21d70042d93f4c4b8e3201d/pkg/controller/cloud/node_controller.go#L323

This (in a healthy case) sends 4 GCE API calls to:
1. get node addresses: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c276a451d64d161b21d70042d93f4c4b8e3201d/pkg/controller/cloud/node_controller.go#L439 (as part of getNodeModifier call)
2. get instance type:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c276a451d64d161b21d70042d93f4c4b8e3201d/pkg/controller/cloud/node_controller.go#L452 (as part of getNodeModifiers call)
3. get instance:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c276a451d64d161b21d70042d93f4c4b8e3201d/pkg/controller/cloud/node_controller.go#L233 (as part of updateNodeAddresses call)
4. get node addresses (again):
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c276a451d64d161b21d70042d93f4c4b8e3201d/pkg/controller/cloud/node_controller.go#L242 (as part of updateNodeAddresses call)

All those requests are read requests and could be replaced by a single call.
We could do that by introducing a simple struct like:
```
type InstanceMetadata struct {
  ProviderID ...
  Type ...
  NodeAddresses ...
}
```
and adding a method (or rather replacing the existing InstanceTypeByProviderID which is used only for this purpose) to Instances cloud-provider interface;
```
func InstanceMetadataByProviderID(...) (*InstanceMetadata, error)
```

With that change, we would be able to replace all that 4 calls with just a single API call.

This would be useful especially for creating large clusters (like 5k nodes), which may saturate the quota for API calls for quite some time.

This is quite significant size of refactoring, though it should be relatively mechanical task to do.

/sig cloud-provider
/sig scalability
/priority important-longterm

/help-wanted

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #89816: unexpected podIP and hostIP in pod

Issue description:
**What happened**:

Unexpected podIP and hostIP in pod, just like
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  ......
status:
  ......
  hostIP: <nil>
  podIP: <nil>
  ......
```

**What you expected to happen**:

This is a host-networking pod, podIP and hostIP in status should be node's internal IP.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Set kubelet's cloud provider to `external`, then set some invalid addresses to node.


**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):  1.14

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: DualStack: basic dual-stack node IP handling
PR description:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind feature

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Makes two related improvements to kubelet node IP handling:

- On bare metal (ie, when there is no `--cloud-provider`), the administrator can now pass a comma-separated pair of IPs via `--node-ip` to manually configure dual-stack `node.status.addresses`. No other scenarios (eg, cloud provider, bare-metal autodetection) are changed.
- On nodes with dual-stack `node.status.addresses` (regardless of how they got them), hostNetwork pods will now have dual-stack `pod.status.podIPs`, allowing the pod to be the target of either a single-stack IPv4 or single-stack IPv6 Service (or, once #91824 merges, a dual-stack Service).

There is ongoing discussion about dual-stack node IPs in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1665, and it probably won't be resolved in time for Enhancement Freeze. However, it seems like there has always been consensus that (a) regardless of what else is possible, it ought to be possible to explicitly specify a dual-stack pair of IPs on bare-metal nodes, (b) regardless of how a node ends up with dual-stack IPs, if it has dual-stack IPs, then that should be reflected in hostNetwork pods. So this PR implements those two things. Additional functionality will presumably come later.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #91940
Fixes #89816 (invalid node IP set by cloud provider causes `"<nil>"` podIP on hostnetwork pod)

**Special notes for your reviewer**:
Currently built on top of #94474 (the first two commits). That can still be reviewed separately, or it can be reviewed as part of this.

Does not conflict with #91824 (dual-stack Services), as this PR only touches kubelet-related things, and that PR does not touch anything kubelet related except a small fix to kubenet (which this PR doesn't touch).

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
In dual-stack bare-metal clusters, you can now pass dual-stack IPs to `kubelet --node-ip`.
eg: `kubelet --node-ip 10.1.0.5,fd01::0005`. This is not yet supported for non-bare-metal
clusters.

In dual-stack clusters where nodes have dual-stack addresses, hostNetwork pods
will now get dual-stack PodIPs.
```

/sig node
/priority important-soon
/assign @thockin

Issue #894: Add a `.Template` set of values into the template engine

Issue description:
Currently we have three top-level objects that are passed into templates:
- `.Chart` contains chart info (essentially the manifest)
- `.Release` contains info about the release
- `.Values` contains the computed values (from the various values.yaml files)

Issue #2224: Helm 2.2.3 not working properly with kubeadm 1.6.1 default RBAC rules

Issue description:
When installing a cluster for the first time using `kubeadm` v1.6.1, the initialization defaults to setting up RBAC controlled access, which messes with permissions needed by Tiller to do installations, scan for installed components, and so on. `helm init` works without issue, but `helm list`, `helm install`, and so on all do not work, citing some missing permission or another.

A work-around for this is to create a service account, add the service account to the tiller deployment, and bind that service account to the ClusterRole `cluster-admin`. If that is how it should work out of the box, then those steps should be part of `helm init`. Ideally, a new ClusterRole should be created based on the privileges of the user instantiating the Tiller instance, but that could get complicated very quickly.

At the very least, there should be some word in the documentation so that users installing helm using the instructions included within won't be wondering why they can't install anything.

Specific steps for my workaround:
```
kubectl create serviceaccount --namespace kube-system tiller
kubectl create clusterrolebinding tiller-cluster-rule --clusterrole=cluster-admin --serviceaccount=kube-system:tiller
kubectl edit deploy --namespace kube-system tiller-deploy #and add the line serviceAccount: tiller to spec/template/spec
```

When you have a repo URL with a path (e.g. `http://example.com/helm`) along with a chart URL (defined in `index.yaml`) which is relative (e.g. `charts/foo-1.2.3.tgz`), the resulting download URL is wrong: `http://example.com/helmchart/foo-1.2.3.tgz`.

PR description:

Issue description:
Helm plugin downloader functionality doesn't currently support sub-commands. This limits how plugin writers can structure their programs. It also makes it incompatible with argument parsing libraries like kingpin since you can't mix top level arguments with other sub-commands. downloaders:
- command: "helm-example download"

apiVersion: v1

**values.yaml**
```yaml
---
```

foo: {{ .Values.unset | required "uset is required!" }}

2019/06/13 16:00:11 [INFO] Missing required value: uset is required!

Currently it will take no action if the desired specified version to be installed is the same as the version available in `PATH`, regardless of what version is found at `HELM_INSTALL_DIR`. What it should do is check the version of `helm` using the binary located at `HELM_INSTALL_DIR` and update the version there if appropriate.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #6452: Helm 3 beta3: go-client caching issue when installing chart resource which is based on a CRD

Issue description:
Output of `helm version`:
```
version.BuildInfo{Version:"v3.0.0-beta.3", GitCommit:"5cb923eecbe80d1ad76399aee234717c11931d9a", GitTreeState:"clean", GoVersion:"go1.12.9"}
```

Output of `kubectl version`:
```
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"15", GitVersion:"v1.15.3", GitCommit:"2d3c76f9091b6bec110a5e63777c332469e0cba2", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2019-08-19T12:36:28Z", GoVersion:"go1.12.9", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/amd64"}
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"15", GitVersion:"v1.15.2", GitCommit:"f6278300bebbb750328ac16ee6dd3aa7d3549568", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2019-08-05T09:15:22Z", GoVersion:"go1.12.5", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
```

**Issue**
When installing a Helm chart which includes a resource from a previously registered CRD (not included in helm chart), Helm throws an error like the following one.

```
Error: apiVersion "test.com/v1alpha1" in reproducer/templates/demo.yaml is not available
```

This problem was already handled in these issues & PR's:
https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/5654
https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/6049

The actual problem still exists. The reason is, that the client-go discovery cache doesn't gets invalidated before installing the chart.

**Reproducer**

Register a CRD out of the scope of Helm.

```
kubectl apply -f - << EOF
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: demos.test.com
spec:
  group: test.com
  names:
    kind: Demo
    listKind: DemoList
    plural: demos
    singular: demo
  scope: Namespaced
  subresources:
    status: {}
  version: v1alpha1
  versions:
  - name: v1alpha1
    served: true
    storage: true
EOF
```

Try to install or template (with --validate) a chart with the following resource.

```
apiVersion: test.com/v1alpha1
kind: Demo
metadata:
  name: default
spec: {}
```

This results in the error.

```
Error: apiVersion "test.com/v1alpha1" in reproducer/templates/demo.yaml is not available
```

After invalidating the client-go discovery cache it works as expected. As a workaround it's possible to invalidate the cache by executing `kubectl api-versions`, which internally invalidates the discovery cache (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/48016/files), before installing the chart.

```
kubectl api-versions
...
helm template testchart --validate
---
# Source: reproducer/templates/demo.yaml
apiVersion: test.com/v1alpha1
kind: Demo
metadata:
  name: default
spec: {}
```

**Possible fix**

Currently Helm internally invalidates the discovery cache only if there are CRD's applied in the context of the Helm chart. (https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/v3.0.0-beta.3/pkg/action/install.go#L131)

A possible solution would be to always invalidate the discovery cache when installing a chart if the mode isn't `clientOnly`.

https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/v3.0.0-beta.3/pkg/action/install.go#L175

```
	if i.ClientOnly {
		// Add mock objects in here so it doesn't use Kube API server
		// NOTE(bacongobbler): used for `helm template`
		i.cfg.Capabilities = chartutil.DefaultCapabilities
		i.cfg.KubeClient = &kubefake.PrintingKubeClient{Out: ioutil.Discard}
		i.cfg.Releases = storage.Init(driver.NewMemory())
	} else {
		// Invalidate the discovery cache here
    }
```


**Related issues and pull requests**
https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/5654
https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/6049

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR description:
We want to force a cache invalidation to ensure that the Capabilities object always has the latest information from the server (Kubernetes server version, available API versions, etc). `kubectl version` forces a cache invalidation every time it's invoked, so this seems like a safe change that is identical to kubectl's behaviour.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #3221: Helm should allow easier "management" of child charts placed manually in `charts`

Issue description:
I have a PR (kubernetes/charts#1719) that uses two subcharts, with a `requirements.yaml` to make it easy to choose whether one or the other is not deployed.  Currently the acceptance test is failing because it does `helm dep up` before trying to install the chart, and with no `repository` line in requirements.yaml `helm dep up` fails.  Declaring the "local" repository causes `helm dep up` to fail a la #2887.  I could eliminate the use of `requirements.yaml` but then I'd have to wrap every template in an `{{- if foo.enabled }}` block, which seems inelegant at best.

It may seem nonsensical to have the source repo be the `charts` directory but in my case it's the direct result of these constraints:

* using subcharts
* wanting to allow subcharts to be turned on or off independently
* wanting that to be easy to maintain

I propose one of the following two fixes:

* `helm dep up` ignores dependencies that have no repo declared instead of throwing an error
* if `helm dep up` sees a dependency source URL that resolves to the `charts` directory of the installing chart, it does not try to download the dependency but checks that it is already present and meets any declared constraints like version requirements, erroring only if those checks fail.

PR title: fix(kube): fix race condition
PR description:
`.Get()` calls `perform()` on a list of infos, populating two shared maps to display the resources fetched. As of #5611 (introduced in 2.15.0), `perform()` now concurrently calls `ResourceActorFunc` concurrently based on GVK, causing a data race condition in `.Get()`.

This fixes that condition by locking the function to ensure these functions run serially for Helm 2 to fix the data race condition. This code has since been refactored out in Helm 3 so it's no longer an issue there.

To verify, run `go test` with the `-race` flag.

closes #6643

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #7377: Using the Helm SDK when no kubeconfig is available

Issue description:
Currently when using helm SDK, a `RESTClientGetter` is needed. This is trivial when a kubeconfig file is available. However when the program only have access to the CA, token/certs and url in memory, it becomes a bit more complicated.

In fact the program needs to implement the following interfaces:
- `ToRESTConfig() (*rest.Config, error)`
- `ToDiscoveryClient() (discovery.CachedDiscoveryInterface, error)`
- `ToRESTMapper() (meta.RESTMapper, error)`

Of course it can still be done with some magic, but then it is also needed to create a new abstraction over the namespace with the `ToRawKubeConfigLoader()` method.

A fix would be to add a `Namespace` field to the kube client in order to lighten a bit the custom implementation written to use Helm3 without a kubeconfig

I have noticed that `helm install/upgrade` tries to resolve all dependencies. Issue description:
The `ValidName` regular expression in `action.go` is from a very old version of Kubernetes.

- Disallows starting with a number, which is now allowed

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #1990: Add lint rule for spec.matchLabels on Deployment

Issue description:
Resources like Deployment, ReplicaSet, and DaemonSet should, as a best practice, declare `selector.matchLabels` rules in their pod template:

https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/tools/kubectl/object-management-using-declarative-config/#defining-controller-selectors-and-podtemplate-labels

Doing so prevents a number of odd-ball cases where pods are not appropriately updated.

We should write a linting rule to catch this case.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: feat: Detect missing selector during lint
PR description:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Make sure to read the Contributing Guide before submitting your PR: https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
2. If this PR closes another issue, add 'closes #<issue number>' somewhere in the PR summary. GitHub will automatically close that issue when this PR gets merged. Alternatively, adding 'refs #<issue number>' will not close the issue, but help provide the reviewer more context.-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

This issue closes #1990 by adding a quick test for `matchLabels` or `matchExpressions` in specific Kubernetes kinds. This was a requested feature because so many Helm issues were being filed because of malformed charts. I don't know if this is any longer necessary. If not, we can probably just close-won't-fix #1990.

Because a chart with no valid selector is _illegal_, this is an error. It catches `matchLabels` and `matchSelectors` (instead of just `selector`) because the requirement is that one of these two most be present. These are the fields frequently left off by chart authors.

Like all other chart lints, this does not enforce anything other than that the strings are present.

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

This change will definitely cause some charts that did not pass before to fail a lint now. However, those charts would have been broken had they been installed.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #8645: "helm version" does not report patch number when compiled outside regular process

Issue description:
Helm version 3.3 breaks semver compatibility because of missing patch version. Tools which rely on a correct version synthax are failing.

(Ex: https://github.com/GoogleContainerTools/skaffold/issues/4711)

The next patch version will fix this problem but it should be considered for the next minor version.

Output of `helm version`:
```
 helm version --client
version.BuildInfo{Version:"v3.3", GitCommit:"", GitTreeState:"", GoVersion:"go1.15"}
```

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Makefile: Fix LDFLAGS overriding
PR description:
When distributions build software it's desriable to have the ability to
define own linker flags, or Go flags. As `-ldflags` defined in `go
build` overrides `-ldflags` defined in the env variable `GOFLAGS`, there
is a distinct need to be able to define new replace the default values
with new ones.

This patch introduces the override directive to the Makefile so we are
able to supply own LDFLAGS from the `make` invocation along with
appending any needed LDFLAGS from the Makefile.

https://ftp.gnu.org/old-gnu/Manuals/make-3.79.1/html_chapter/make_6.html#SEC66

Fixes #8645

Signed-off-by: Morten Linderud <morten@linderud.pw>

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

```bash
λ helm » make LDFLAGS="-s -w -linkmode external" GOFLAGS="-buildmode=pie -trimpath"
GO111MODULE=on go build -buildmode=pie -trimpath -tags '' -ldflags '-s -w -linkmode external -X helm.sh/helm/v3/internal/version.version=v3.3.0 -X helm.sh/helm/v3/internal/version.metadata= -X helm.sh/helm/v3/internal/version.gitCommit=8a4aeec08d67a7b84472007529e8097ec3742105 -X helm.sh/helm/v3/internal/version.gitTreeState=dirty' -o /home/fox/Git/prosjekter/Go/helm/bin/helm ./cmd/helm
```

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #1222: Manually kill containerd-shim when container is paused causes other docker command block forever

Issue description:
**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
Run the following script:
```bash
1     #!/bin/bash
2     i=0
3     while true; do
4             ((i++))
5             containerid=`docker run -tid ubuntu`
6             docker pause $containerid
7             kill -9 `docker top $containerid | awk 'NR==2{print $3}'`     # get shim pid of this container and kill it
8             docker top $containerid
9             echo "$i:success!"
10     done
```

**Describe the results you received:**
The script gets block within 10 seconds, it blocks at L8.

**Describe the results you expected:**
No block.

**Additional information you deem important (e.g. issue happens only occasionally):**
After [containerd/containerd #1111](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/1111), kill shim of a paused container will first resume this container, then this container is killed. But when the the script blocks, I find the container is still paused. `handleSigkilledShim()` returns at https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/v0.2.x/runtime/process.go#L306, so the following `p.container.Resume()` is not reached.

That is to say, when `exit` pipe is closed since shim is killed, we can still see shim for a while. I have tried to add a sleep(10 milliseconds) before `e := unix.Kill(p.cmd.Process.Pid, 0)`, then the above script won't block for a long time.


@mlaventure @coolljt0725 Any ideas about this issue?

**Description**

CRI plugin does have [a stop function](https://github.com/containerd/cri-containerd/blob/master/pkg/server/service.go#L281). It stops containerd event monitor and the streaming server and possibly more components in the future.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #2683: Edge cases where containerd would fail to re-pull an image from a private GCR repository

Issue description:
**Description**

I'm not sure whether this is considered a bug or working intended, but thought it might still be worth reporting.

When containerd (client) pulls an image, it tries to pull without authentication first. If the request fails with a 401 error, containerd retries the request with authentication information. This works fine in normal cases, but I can fabricate a case that would fail consistently. For example, if I delete an image layer from the content store manually, then try to repull the same image from GCR, the request will fail with a 403 error. The reason is that containerd skips fetching the image manifest (which is already present on the node), where it usually relies on to authenticate.

1. containerd resolves the image.
2. containerd tries to fetch the image manifest, but found it in the content store. (no real fetching, no authentication)
3. containerd attempts to fetch the children digests from the manifest without authentication
    - GCR redirects (302) the anonymous request to the GCS bucket
    - GCS rejects the anonymous request and returns 403.
4. containerd aborts the pull operation after seeing 403.


**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
1. Use `crictl` to pull an image from a private GCR repository
2. Delete a (non-image-manifest) layer/blob of the pulled image from the content store
3. Try repulling the same image.

**Describe the results you received:**
```
pulling image failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to pull and unpack image "gcr.io/k8s-authenticated-test/serve-hostname-amd64:1.0": httpReaderSeeker: failed open: unexpected status code https://gcr.io/v2/k8s-authenticated-test/serve-hostname-amd64/blobs/sha256:080afe3806dc31a89e0cb073f487f203c093bcec0229f0c61342891d20f3b5c5: 403 Forbidden
```
**Describe the results you expected:**

containerd re-pull the image successfully.

**Output of `containerd --version`:**

```
containerd github.com/containerd/containerd v1.2.0-beta.2 ce243288e27971e324363de8f322d221635a852
```

Deleting an image layer from the content store without deleting the manifest should not happen with normal workflows, so maybe it's okay to ignore the edge case. On the other hand, if we want to tackle that, here are some random ideas: 1) try authenticating after receiving 403, or 2) re-use the authentication information from the resolver, 3) ask GCS to return 401 instead, and 4) always re-pull the manifest(?).

This doesn't happen with images using Docker schema 1 manifest. Containerd will always try pulling down the schema 1 manifest for reasons unknown to me.

/cc @Random-Liu

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Update Docker resolver to pass in Authorizer interface
PR description:
This creates an authorizer interface which can be shared across multiple requests and more configurable for setting the authorization. This fixes a bug today which doesn't case sharing of tokens between resolve and fetch due to creation of a different base object which caches. Additionally this change moves the implementation closer to being focused on the OCI distribution specification while keeping the Docker specific authorization as a separate component.

An additional change can be done later to remove the credentials function after the callers have updated. There is also an additional change to allow the host/scheme specification to be more robust and have better support for mirrored configuration without needing to create multiple instances for each host. I wanted to keep that separate from the authorization component.

Fixes #1005
Fixes #2683

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #4301: Slow Windows container start time when using servercore image

Issue description:
We are seeing slower launch times of Windows containers using servercore images (or images derived from servercore). Upon investigation, this appears to be due to the C:\Windows\System32\CatRoot directory modification timestamp being different from the value in the container. This causes the Windows catdb to be rebuilt on container launch, which impacts container startup time.

We have root caused this to an issue in the Windows layer unpack code in Microsoft/hcsshim. When unpacking a delta layer, the directory timestamps are not correctly reset to their proper values after removing files removed via whiteout. We are working on a fix, and will then need to revendor Microsoft/hcsshim. We are tracking the issue on the hcsshim side via https://github.com/microsoft/hcsshim/issues/830.

Note that this bug could have other impact as well, as in general it can cause delta layer directory timestamps to be incorrect. The primary impact we have observed is the slow start time with servercore container images.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #1186: check PD list validation

Issue description:
pd1 is a standalone cluster(a), pd2 and pd3 is the other cluster(b). We have many TiKVs, when the TiKV bootstraps, it randomly selects a PD to connect, so we may have two TiKVs which have same store ID (1) but belong to different clusters (a and b). We use 1a and 1b to distinguish them.
When 1b is down and 1a restarts, it may connect to cluster b because it chooses the PD in PD list randomly. Badly, 1a can join the cluster b, can communicate with other TiKVs in the cluster b too and we will meet data corruption here.

When we start tikv with a pd list like `pd1:2379,pd2:2379,pd3:2379`, we must check these PDs are all in the same cluster. E,g, we can use `members` API to get all PD members. If we get pd1 and pd2 only in the response, we can think PD3 is not a valid PD. But here we should also consider the condition that PD3 has already been removed.

/cc @huachaohuang

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: pd: validate PD list
PR description:
`validate_pd_list` only accepts PD endpoints that are in the same PD cluster. It treats a removed PD as an invalied PD node. ~~It only validates once at the beginning of raftkv startup.~~ It validates the list every time when the tikv trys to connect a PD.

---

Let's say there are two PD clusters, one consists three nodes, and the other is a standlone node. Details:

```
cluster-id: 1
pd1 client urls: "127.0.0.1:12379"
pd2 client urls: "127.0.0.1:22379"
pd3 client urls: "127.0.0.1:32379"
```

```
cluster-id: 1
pd1 client urls: "127.0.0.1:42379"
```

Following are cases tested so far:

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #4389: Try to remove codegen from tikv-server, etc.

Issue description:
During my profiling I've noticed that the codegen for tikv-server takes almost as long as the codegen for the tikv lib. Codegen being the time it takes for rustc to emit llvm IR.

This is surprising since the tikv-server binary contains very little code.

My guess is there's a ton of generics instantiation in the crate, which would be duplicated in the other bins as well, and maybe in the lib.

Move as much code as reasonable directly into the library and see if that has any effect on the codegen time in tikv-server, and any effect on the overall build time.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Moving code from bin/util into tikv, and crate docs
PR description:
## What have you changed? (mandatory)

This moves most of the `src/bin/util` code and most of `src/bin/tikv-server.rs` into the `tikv` library. In addition to making it easier to use the library to create a tikv server, it also reduces the amount of utility coded that is recompiled between the three binaries.

This is a follow up to my [previous cleanup pr](https://github.com/tikv/tikv/pull/4513). It does a number of things.

It started out as a documentation patch, and I add some basic crate docs. Then I started documenting some of the configuration methods, but found I wanted more of the setup code from tikv-server, so that it would be easier to write examples.

So then I pulled in some commits for https://github.com/tikv/tikv/issues/4389, moving all of `src/bin/util` into the `tikv` library, and then the setup code from tikv-server. Now it should be easy to show documentation examples for the API.

Moving code from the bins into tikv will reduce the amount of compilation work, but won't reduce serial compilation time.

It is getting pretty big, so I hope to land it before continuing.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #6366: Two overlapped snapshot may be applied together which may cause panic or loss of data

Issue description:
Theoretically, the pending_snapshot_region and region_ranges in StoreMeta should prevent overlapped snapshots.
But it is problematic sometimes.

At each end of raftstore's batch, the received snapshot region ids in this batch are removed from pending_snapshot_regions.
Most of the time, this removed region will be updated to region_ranges, so it can still prevent overlapped snapshots.

However, a pending snapshot may not be handled for some reason. e.g. waiting for its source region to destroy.
In this case, this snapshot's region range is larger than the original range and is not updated to region_ranges.

After its source region is destroyed, another overlapped snapshot B is received. (overlap with its source region and maybe from a new peer)
Two overlapped snapshot will be applied together and break the data in this range.
It may cause some serious problems. e.g. panic, loss of data.

The simple fix method is just remove handled snapshot region id not all received snapshot region id in this batch.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: raftstore: make destroy overlapped regions and apply snapshot atomically
PR description:
Signed-off-by: Liqi Geng <gengliqiii@gmail.com>


###  What have you changed?

The operation of destroying overlapped regions and applying snapshot must be atomic, otherwise, it may cause a target peer can't find its corresponding source peer when applying `CommitMerge` log in extreme cases.

A tikv may crash after a target peer does not become `Applying` state which means it will not apply snapshot after this tikv restarts. But its corresponding source peers may have destroyed.
After this tikv restarts, a new leader may send logs to this target peer in some cases.
Then the panic will happen because it can not find its source peers when applying `CommitMerge` log.

In addition to the above problem, this PR also fix https://github.com/tikv/tikv/issues/6366 and https://github.com/tikv/tikv/issues/7002.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #7364: Txn: collapsing the rollback record of pessimistic lock could cause inconsistency

Issue description:
## Bug Report

### What version of TiKV are you using?

master

### What did happened?

A false assertion is found in: https://github.com/tikv/tikv/blob/c3f9fba14b04811e77614bcd50007bad17e251c3/src/storage/mvcc/txn.rs#L684-L691

where pessimistic transactions may commit successfully even when some of its keys it prewrited are rollbacked by cleanup-resolve procedural invoked by a duplicated cleanup command, which is sent before for cleaning up the pessimistic lock.

### Steps to reproduce

Assume that we have three clients {c1, c2, c3} and two keys {k1, k2}:

1. Pessimistic client c1 acquires a pessimistic lock on k1(primary), k2. But the command for k1 is lost at this point.
2. Optimistic client c2 requires to clean up the lock on k2
3. k1 is rollbacked and a write record `("rollback", c1_start_ts, not_protected)` is written into k1 (not_protected because the lock on k1 is missing), and a `resolve(primary=k1, ts=c1_start_ts)`(*1) is sent but lost at this point.
4. Client c3 prewrites k1
5. Client c2 requires to clean up the lock on k1
6. k1 is rollbacked and the rollback write record is **collapsed** to `("rollback", c3_start_ts, protected/not_protected)`
7. Client c1 retries to lock on k1
8. k1 is locked by c1
9. Client c1 prewrites k1, k2
10. k1, k2 are prewrited by c1, and c1 received the prewrite succeed response
11. The lost resolve command (*1) in step 3 is received by k2, therefore k2 is rollbacked
12. Client c1 commit k1
13. k1 is committed, while k2 is rollbacked

Then atomic guarantee is broken.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR description:
Signed-off-by: Dian Luo <andylokandy@hotmail.com>

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #7484: The unified read pool should not use start_ts as task id

Issue description:
## Bug Report

### What version of TiKV are you using?

4.0-beta.2 and up

### What operating system and CPU are you using?

Unrelated

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a transaction, run a big query (for example `SELECT COUNT(*)` from a big table).
2. Start some other big queries.
3. While those big queries are in process, run a small query (for example a point select) in the transaction started in 1.

### What did you expect?

The small query finishes quickly.

### What did happened?

Because we use start_ts as the task id, the priority of the small query is lowered by the previously executed big query, thus it may take some time to finish. I don't think it's a reasonable strategy.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: *: use given task id or random number as task id
PR description:
- [x] Depends on https://github.com/pingcap/kvproto/pull/604

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: Closes #7484

Problem Summary:

It's not suitable in all cases to use start ts as the task id for the unified read pool. For example, in the same transaction, a big query is executed and the following point selects are also downgraded.

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

https://github.com/pingcap/kvproto/pull/604 adds `task_id` to kv context. We can use it to generate a better task id instead of using start_ts in coprocessor.
Task id tends to be generated in serial. The algorithm is replacing the high 16 bits of start ts (which is not so representative) with the low 16-bits of the given task id.
This PR also changes to let all storage tasks use random number as task id. These tasks tend to end fast so we don't bother to give them a meaningful task id. (Maybe we can do it in the future)

### Related changes

- Need to cherry-pick to the release branch

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

PR title: Improve robustness of Backup/Restore involving external_storage
PR description:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to TiKV!

If you haven't already, please read TiKV's [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/tikv/tikv/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) document.

If you're unsure about anything, just ask; somebody should be along to answer within a day or two.

PR Title Format:
1. module [, module2, module3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed
-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #7375, close #7850, close #7880, close tidb-challenge-program/bug-hunting-issue#72

Problem Summary:

The backup/restore did not have timeout and retry. This causes a single spurious network error to either catastrophically kill the entire BR task or block the BR thread pool forever.

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

1. ("Restore" supports retrying externally through pingcap/br#298, so for now we're not going to implement retry for "Restore").
2. The "Backup" gRPC produces a stream, which cannot be retried externally. Therefore, we implemented retry directly in the backup service (`ExternalStorage::write` in particular) to fix #7850.
3. The produced backup file can have size up to 135 MiB. This is not a good idea to retry the upload entirely. So we implemented [Multipart Upload](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/mpuoverview.html) on S3. Unfortunately `tame-gcs` does not support resumable upload EmbarkStudios/tame-gcs#24 so this won't work for GCS. (This also fix #7375.)
    * Unfortunately, we need to copy the SST file into memory and clone several times in order to retry.
4. We have also replaced `reqwest` by `hyper` so those `convert_request` and `convert_response` are no longer needed.
5. For "Restore", we added a timeout around `ExternalStorage::read`, so that a stuck download won't block the thread pool forever, to fix #7880.

### Related changes

- Need to cherry-pick to the release branch

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test
- Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)
    * Backup and restore against a `minio` S3 storage.

Side effects

- Performance regression
    - Consumes more MEM: Backup may need to copy the entire SST file several times.
    - Multi-part upload and retrying would produce many more requests per file.

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

* Improved robustness of backup and restore for S3 and GCS storage.

2. *: what's changed

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #7375, close #7850, close #7880, close tidb-challenge-program/bug-hunting-issue#72

Problem Summary:

The backup/restore did not have timeout and retry. This causes a single spurious network error to either catastrophically kill the entire BR task or block the BR thread pool forever.

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

1. ("Restore" supports retrying externally through pingcap/br#298, so for now we're not going to implement retry for "Restore").
2. The "Backup" gRPC produces a stream, which cannot be retried externally. Therefore, we implemented retry directly in the backup service (`ExternalStorage::write` in particular) to fix #7850.
3. The produced backup file can have size up to 135 MiB. This is not a good idea to retry the upload entirely. So we implemented [Multipart Upload](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/mpuoverview.html) on S3. Unfortunately `tame-gcs` does not support resumable upload EmbarkStudios/tame-gcs#24 so this won't work for GCS. (This also fix #7375.)
    * Unfortunately, we need to copy the SST file into memory and clone several times in order to retry.
4. We have also replaced `reqwest` by `hyper` so those `convert_request` and `convert_response` are no longer needed.
5. For "Restore", we added a timeout around `ExternalStorage::read`, so that a stuck download won't block the thread pool forever, to fix #7880.

### Related changes

- Need to cherry-pick to the release branch

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test
- Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)
    * Backup and restore against a `minio` S3 storage.

Side effects

- Performance regression
    - Consumes more MEM: Backup may need to copy the entire SST file several times.
    - Multi-part upload and retrying would produce many more requests per file.

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

* Improved robustness of backup and restore for S3 and GCS storage.

PR title: backup,config: set backup thread pool size via config instead of gRPC (#8193)
PR description:
cherry-pick #8193 to release-4.0

---

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close pingcap/br#394, close #8076.

Problem Summary:

### What is changed and how it works?

This is the companion PR of pingcap/br#396.

In #5553, the `backup` component gained ability to an adjustable thread pool size. The size is provided via the incoming gRPC request. Given [how the ThreadPool is implemented in TiKV](https://github.com/tikv/tikv/blob/b45e052df8fb5d66aa8b3a77b5c992ddbfbb79df/components/tikv_util/src/threadpool.rs#L204-L219), a user can easily (accidentally) DoS all TiKV servers by setting the thread pool size to a huge number like 2<sup>32</sup>-1.

Furthermore, when we provide the thread pool size through gRPC, the backup client (BR) must determine the suitable concurrency number in some ad-hoc way.

This PR solves both issue by moving the thread pool size back as a TiKV config:

```toml
[backup]
num-threads = 24
```

The default value is set to (0.75 × Number of CPUs) to better utilize the available resources. The value can still be dynamically configured, but given this more practical default value it should be much less needed.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #8216: Reset missing tick counter when receiving the vote msg may lead to slow leader election

Issue description:
In hibernate region, the `missing_tick` is used for recording the raft tick count. If the peer's state becomes chaotic, the missing ticks will be called for `missing_tick` times.

https://github.com/tikv/tikv/blob/4a75902f266fbbc064f0c19a2a681cfe66511bc3/components/raftstore/src/store/fsm/peer.rs#L962-L971

By default, if this peer is hibernated, the `missing_tick` should be 9.

https://github.com/tikv/tikv/blob/4a75902f266fbbc064f0c19a2a681cfe66511bc3/components/raftstore/src/store/fsm/peer.rs#L1114-L1117
In `reset_raft_tick` functions, the `missing_tick` is reset to zero, which may lead to a slow leader election when the old leader is dead, namely, more round of election timeout.

When an old leader A is dead, follower B may become chaotic quicker than follower C.
Then follower B will tick for `missing_tick` times immediately and may send vote msg to follower C.

If follower C receives the vote msg before running `missing_tick`. It will refuse this vote because of the code in raft-rs.
https://github.com/tikv/raft-rs/blob/91d883287317e7a7ca18acbab6b405d4168b3b73/src/raft.rs#L1109-L1137

If so, both two peers need to wait for the next election timeout to choose a new leader.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

messages.content: A repository contains the following reported issue: Issue #8486: Too many rocksdb tombstone may slow batch-get Issue description: In the case, there are a lot of deletes for a range on the transaction level. Once GCed, it leads to a lot of tombstone marks in rocksdb. It is invisible, but iterating on them does have the same overhead as iterating on visible keys. So when batch-get on the GCed keys, it calls `writecf.seek(key)` for each key and needs to iterate over a lot of tombstones for every key internally which hurts performance greatly. Also, coprocessor may suffer the same issue. Some possible solution: - use `prefix_seek` and `prefix_same_as_start` - set `max-skippable-internal-keys=1` for `writecf.seek(key + ts)`. If it encounters a tombstone, it is enough to ensure the key is deleted at this version(without collapse rollback). So it can abort the seek directly, instead of seeking the next visible key. - sort the keys of batch-get, and`PointGetter` records the key of the last `writecf.seek()`. If the recorded_key > now_key then now_key must be deleted. So it won't seek the range with lots of tombstones again and again. - Use rocksdb single delete to relieve(Can't solve it completely) A pull request was created to resolve it: PR title: storage: Optimize seek write for many tombstones PR description: ### What problem does this PR solve? optimize seek write when there are too many tombstones. Fix https://github.com/tikv/tikv/issues/8486 ### What is changed and how it works? Three optimizations: - for batch-get and coprocessor(point-get), use prefix_seek and prefix_same_as_start to get seek every key for write cf, so it can skip tombstones of other keys. - for prewrite, when calculating `has_data_in_range` use `max-skippable-internals-keys` to avoid seek too many tombstones. - check key order before calling `near_seek` for `ScanMode::Mixed` which save one seek() and several prev() calls #### batch-get before and after ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13497871/91380907-b33b5e80-e858-11ea-96ef-349b27dd69c7.png) #### prewrite before and after (before has no tombstone statistics for seek, actually there are a lot) ### Related changes - PR to update `pingcap/docs`/`pingcap/docs-cn`: - PR to update `pingcap/tidb-ansible`: - Need to cherry-pick to the release branch ### Check List Tests - Unit test ### Release note - Optimize seek write for many tombstones Merged upstream at: 2020-10-27T10:47:23Z PR size: +391 additions, -32 deletions, 11 files changed, 9 commits Analyze the issue and explain what problem it reports and how the linked pull request addresses it. A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #8229: MvccTxn can't make use of near_seek

Issue description:
## Bug Report

`MvccTxn` always uses `seek` to find write records. The reason is `MvccReader` in it always creates a new write cursor:
https://github.com/tikv/tikv/blob/11cbf057ba8dec3a0833a9948b5ae9ec54d6113d/src/storage/mvcc/reader/reader.rs#L129-L145

It's better to use `next` to get older versions in some cases. For example, in https://github.com/tikv/tikv/issues/7024, you can see 578k seeks per second. Please be careful with prefix seek in rocksdb, it can't guarantee a total order of all keys, but only keys for the same prefix.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: txn: make use of near_seek for write-cf
PR description:
Signed-off-by: youjiali1995 <zlwgx1023@gmail.com>

PR Title Format:

2. *: what's changed
-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #8229  <!-- REMOVE this line if no issue to close -->

Problem Summary:

`MvccTxn` doesn't make use of `near_seek`. It creates a write cursor for every seek which may cost a lot if many versions exist.

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

Add a single key mode for `MvccReader` which uses a single write cursor for each user key. When the current key is changed, a new write cursor is created to guarantee the total order of all keys due to prefix seek. This check involves a key comparison for every seek, but the cost is in a single-digit nanosecond.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #11606: How to prevent user from executing GC in container of registry/registryctl

Issue description:
As from Harbor v2.0, `tag` is maintained in Harbor instead of back end registry(distribution), which leads to the valid images in Harbor with tags but without tags in the registry.

Therefore, Harbor disables its GC job to delete the untagged manifest when to call registry GC CLI.

But, how can we prevent a user from executing GC CLI with enabling delete untagged manifest option in the container of registry and regsitryctl.

If the user executes GC with the option, it should be a catastrophic event as GC will remove most of the valid images from the backend storage and no way to restore.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

Fixes #11606

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #12827: Fix negative repo ID in artifact table if the repo exists in repository table

Issue description:
In 1.x -> 2.0 migration the repo id of an artifact may be set to negative:

```
/*set the media type*/
UPDATE artifact AS art
    SET type='IMAGE', repository_id=repo.repository_id,
    manifest_media_type=blob.content_type,
    media_type=(
    CASE
        /*v2 manifest*/
        WHEN blob.content_type='application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json' THEN
            'application/vnd.docker.container.image.v1+json'
        /*manifest list*/
        WHEN blob.content_type='application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json' THEN
            'application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json'
        /*v1 manifest*/
        ELSE
            'application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v1+prettyjws'
    END
    )
    FROM repository AS repo, blob AS blob
    WHERE art.repo=repo.name AND art.digest=blob.digest;
/*
It's a workaround for issue https://github.com/goharbor/harbor/issues/11754
The phenomenon is the repository data is gone, but artifacts belong to the repository are still there.
To set the repository_id to a negative, and cannot duplicate.
*/
UPDATE artifact SET repository_id = 0-artifact.id, type='IMAGE', media_type='UNKNOWN', manifest_media_type='UNKNOWN' WHERE repository_id IS NULL;
```

This assume the `repository_id IS NULL`  only happens when there's no corresponding record in the repository table, however, it may also happen when there are inconsistencies between blob table and artifact table.

We should reset the "repo_id" of these records to positive if the repository with the same name exist in repository table.

PR title: middleware/secondary: fix crash with no zone

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #1678: plugin/forward: make read timeout configurable

Issue description:
The recently added dynamic timeout feature (#1659) may give worse results than fixed timeout under some circumstances, e.g. at high load when upstream servers are overloaded. Dynamic timeout allows us re-sending unanswered queries faster, and this could be a problem, because we make upstream server load even higher.

In my tests I saw RTT (round trip time) as minimal as 10μs. For comparison, transmission of 50 bytes (400 bits) over 100Mbit network takes about 4μs. So, we can easily catch timeout at the moment when message was partially read which results in truncated messages

Therefore, I propose to introduce minimal timeout. The reason why we added dynamic timeout feature is to have more attempts to re-send query (probably to different upstreams) during limited period (5 seconds).  Even if we set minimal timeout to 200ms we will get around 25 attempts which is quite enough. No sense to retry faster and create additional server load.

I propose to add a timeout option to forward plugin like below
```
forward .:53 {
    timeout MAX MIN RATIO WEIGHT
}

```
If user specifies only the first parameter (**MAX**) then dynamic timeout will not be used

**MAX** - maximum read timeout which is currently defined by constant `timeout `
https://github.com/coredns/coredns/blob/e671e22e657b2fcb1580abd311e9c340b20b9e96/plugin/forward/proxy.go#L93

**MIN** - minimum read timeout. Timeout is based on average RTT but cannot be less than MIN
**RATIO** - desired timeout/RTT ratio. I.e. timeout will be calculated as (average  RTT) * RATIO
**WEIGHT** - defines how much average RTT is influenced by current RTT, i.e. avgRTT = avgRTT + (newRTT-avgRTT)/WEIGHT like in function below
https://github.com/coredns/coredns/blob/e671e22e657b2fcb1580abd311e9c340b20b9e96/plugin/forward/connect.go#L27-L30

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #1578: [jaeger-query] Leading zeros stripped from trace IDs

Issue description:
<!--
Welcome to the Jaeger project! 👋🎉

- Please search for existing issues to avoid creating duplicate bugs/feature requests.
- Please be respectful and considerate of others when commenting on issues.
- Please provide as much information as possible so we all understand the issue.
- If you only have a question, you may get a faster response by asking in
    - our chat room https://gitter.im/jaegertracing/Lobby, or
    - the forum https://groups.google.com/d/forum/jaeger-tracing
    (but please don't double post)
-->

## Requirement - what kind of business use case are you trying to solve?

I would like to view traces in Jaeger UI where the trace ID has leading 0s.

## Problem - what in Jaeger blocks you from solving the requirement?

When jaeger-query returns data for traces where there are leading 0s in the trace ID, the leading 0s are stripped from the trace ID, within the data. E.g. for a trace with ID `0123`, all of the spans returned refer to trace ID `123`.

For each trace returned by jaeger-query, this applies to:

* The trace ID on the root of the trace data object
* The trace ID fields in each span
* The trace ID fields in internal references

## Proposal - what do you suggest to solve the problem or improve the existing situation?

The zeros should not be stripped.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Do not remove leading zeros in trace ID hex string
PR description:
Resolves #1578 and probably #1951

## Motivation

Among randomly generated and uniformly distributed trace IDs, only 1/16th of them start with 0 followed by a significant digit, 1/256th start with two 0s, and so on in decreasing geometric progression. Therefore, trimming the leading 0s is a very modest optimization on the size of the data being transmitted or stored.

However, trimming 0s leads to ambiguities when the IDs are used as correlations with other monitoring systems, such as logging, that treat the IDs as opaque strings and cannot establish the equivalence between padded and unpadded IDs. It is also incompatible with W3C Trace Context and Zipkin B3 format, both of which include all leading 0s, so an application instrumented with OpenTelemetry SDKs may be logging different trace ID strings than application instrumented with Jaeger SDKs (related issue #1657).

Open question: this change may prevent ES backend from reading the old traces if their IDs had leading zeroes, because previously the zeroes were not added to string representation, and now they are. Roughly one in 16 traces will be affected.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #2037: Expose Samara Kafka producer/consumer configurations to command line.

Issue description:
## Requirement - what kind of business use case are you trying to solve?

We are using Jaeger with Ingester.  On Collector, we are setting SPAN_STORAGE_TYPE=kafka.  We would like to tune Kafka configurations for performance.  The default Kafka Samara config is resulting in over 150% CPU usage on Kafka broker for just 40k spans per minute.

## Problem - what in Jaeger blocks you from solving the requirement?
Jaeger provided these producer settings
```
      --kafka.producer.authentication string          Authentication type used to authenticate with kafka cluster. e.g. none, kerberos, tls (default "none")
      --kafka.producer.brokers string                 The comma-separated list of kafka brokers. i.e. '127.0.0.1:9092,0.0.0:1234' (default "127.0.0.1:9092")
      --kafka.producer.compression string             (experimental) Type of compression (none, gzip, snappy, lz4, zstd) to use on messages (default "none")
      --kafka.producer.compression-level int          (experimental) compression level to use on messages. gzip = 1-9 (default = 6), snappy = none, lz4 = 1-17 (default = 9), zstd = -131072 - 22 (default = 3)
      --kafka.producer.encoding string                Encoding of spans ("json" or "protobuf") sent to kafka. (default "protobuf")
      --kafka.producer.kerberos.config-file string    Path to Kerberos configuration. i.e /etc/krb5.conf (default "/etc/krb5.conf")
      --kafka.producer.kerberos.keytab-file string    Path to keytab file. i.e /etc/security/kafka.keytab (default "/etc/security/kafka.keytab")
      --kafka.producer.kerberos.password string       The Kerberos password used for authenticate with KDC
      --kafka.producer.kerberos.realm string          Kerberos realm
      --kafka.producer.kerberos.service-name string   Kerberos service name (default "kafka")
      --kafka.producer.kerberos.use-keytab            Use of keytab instead of password, if this is true, keytab file will be used instead of password
      --kafka.producer.kerberos.username string       The Kerberos username used for authenticate with KDC
      --kafka.producer.protocol-version string        Kafka protocol version - must be supported by kafka server
      --kafka.producer.required-acks string           (experimental) Required kafka broker acknowledgement. i.e. noack, local, all (default "local")
      --kafka.producer.tls.ca string                  Path to the TLS CA for the Kafka connection
      --kafka.producer.tls.cert string                Path to the TLS Certificate for the Kafka connection
      --kafka.producer.tls.key string                 Path to the TLS Key for the Kafka connection
      --kafka.producer.topic string
```
Setting `--kafka.producer.required-acks` to `noack` helps a little, reducing CPU usage on Kafka broker by 8%.  We experimented setting github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pkg/kafka/producer/config.go with the following parameters.  It resulted in 10 times improvement in Kafka broker CPU usage.
```
        saramaConfig.Producer.Flush.Bytes = 128000
        saramaConfig.Producer.Flush.Frequency = time.Duration(1 * time.Second)
```

## Proposal - what do you suggest to solve the problem or improve the existing situation?
At a minimum, Jaeger should expose the above 2 settings to the command line.  Ideally Jaeger should expose all producer/consumer configurations.
Given that each Kafka client has it's own naming for configurations.  I would suggest Jaeger use Kafka's official parameter names for it's client.  For example, `saramaConfig.Producer.Flush.Bytes` should be exposed as `batch.size` and `saramaConfig.Producer.Flush.Frequency` should be exposed as `linger.ms`
<!-- It's ok if you don't have one. -->

The default Samara Kafka client writes to Kafka broker for every single span received.

Samara Kafka client has options to enable batching.  These options needed to be exposed
to the command for performance tuning. The option names matches official Kafka documentation and
not specific to Samara.

PR title: Mons started as a replicaset instead of directly as a pod
PR description:
One replicaset is created for each mon, with a replica count of 1. The mons are assigned to a node, which is critical for recovery of the mon. When a new pod is started, the same metadata dir will be available on the same node as long as a hostDir was specified. If no hostDir was specified then quorum is required to restore that monitor. Issue #1701: Flex driver conflicts when multiple rook system namespaces are running

Issue description:
When there are multiple rook namespaces running, we observe that the flex volume drivers for the namespaces will conflict.
- The agent pods will be watching the same unix socket
- If one namespace is terminated, the unix socket will be deleted from under the agent in the other namespace

The latter is an issue commonly in the integration tests running in jenkins. Immediately after one test suite is removed, another suite starts. The removal might actually take several seconds to complete and will remove the socket from under the new namespace.

To allow multiple namespaces to use the flex driver, we will need to base the name of the flex driver on the namespace where the operator/agent pair are running. Since the drivers would be registered under rook.io, we wouldn't have to worry about conflicting with any other driver.

Multiple rook system namespaces cannot be currently run because of the conflict between using the same flex driver. This change creates a driver name based on the namespace to avoid that conflict. For backward compatibility, the agent will also watch the unix socket for the old driver name (rook).

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #1389: Improve Rook's Security Model

Issue description:
Rook currently uses multiple namespaces and service accounts. The rook operator can create and delete namespaces, service accounts, roles and role bindings on the fly. As a result rook requires a *very* privileged service account (see [here](https://github.com/rook/rook/blob/master/cluster/examples/kubernetes/rook-operator.yaml#L9)).

For production clusters this not going to work. We need to explore running in a mode where we do not have privileges to destroy the entire cluster. Also creating a deleting namespace is not necessarily something that every cluster-admin is going to want us to do.

If a cluster-admin wants to set policies (PSP, SCC, resource quotas, etc.) they need to be able to control which service accounts and namespaces Rook uses. Creating namespaces and service accounts on the fly means that these policies would need to be dynamically applied too.

This is a complicated issue but it's one that we should front load. Its come up in the following places #1314 #1337 #1348 #1211 and possible more. Also discussion on twitter here: https://twitter.com/the_sttts/status/945077544587616257

 I'm going to write a design doc and link it here when its ready.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Refactor cluster roles for minimal rbac access
PR description:
Signed-off-by: travisn <tnielsen@redhat.com>

Description of your changes:
Per the [security model](https://github.com/rook/rook/blob/master/design/security-model.md#proposed-changes) proposal:
- There is one serviceAccount per namespace, one for `rook-system` and one for each cluster that is created: `rook-ceph-cluster`.
- The operator, agent, and discovery daemons all run with the `rook-system` service account
- The OSD daemon runs with the `rook-ceph-cluster` service account. Other cluster daemons (mon, mgr, mds, rgw) run with the default service account since they do not require access to k8s resources.
- Rook no longer creates service accounts, cluster roles, roles, etc. These must be created by the admin.

Differing from the security model spec, a ClusterRoleBinding was needed for several resources:
- Rook CRDs: Watched and handled across all namespaces
- Pods: The agent needs to analyze pods for fencing
- PVs & PVCs: The operator provisioner needs to create, delete, list, etc
- Nodes: Used to determine on which nodes to place mons
- Storage classes: watched by the operator

The `rook-ceph-core` role was created for the namespace-specific resources and the `rook-ceph-global` role was created for cluster-wide resources.

Issue #1752: Ceph daemon names should match k8s pod names where possible

Issue description:
To make it easier to troubleshoot the Ceph daemons, the pod names should match the daemon names wherever possible.

### Stateless daemons

#### MDS
The name of the mds will be the same as the pod name. MDS is stateless therefore maintaining a consistent name is not needed.

Currently the mds daemon name only consists of the random k8s pod suffix such as `fn72k`, which means now we would use more of the pod name. If the pod name is `rook-ceph-mds-myfs-5f8556bd99-fn72k`, the daemon would be `mds.myfs-5f8556bd99-fn72k`.

#### RGW
Clients need to know the service name rather than the pod name. The rgw service will start with the service name for the `rgw_zone` and `rgw_zonegroup` settings. Need to investigate if the daemon name is exposed in the service map.

#### Mgr
There is only one mgr in Rook named `rook-ceph-mgr`. The mgr name needs to match the service name rather than the pod name. The service name is constant so that clients can connect to the dashboard and prometheus metrics. There is no need for multiple mgrs since Kubernetes will failover the pod automatically. The name is currently `rook-ceph-mgr0` so we can remove the `0` suffix.

The pod can be queried with a label:
```
kubectl -n rook-ceph get pod -l app=rook-ceph-mgr
```

### Mons and OSDs

#1656 will name the osds to match the OSD IDs and #1751 will take care of renaming the mons to follow this pattern. However, the mon and osd pod names will still have a random k8s suffix in addition to the daemon name. For example, the daemon name and deployment name for a mon would be `rook-ceph-mon-a`, while its pod name might be `rook-ceph-mon-a-5f8556bd99-gjpd8`.

The recommended way to work with the mon and osd pods will to be use labels. This example shows how a specific mon or osd pod might be queried.
```
kubectl -n rook-ceph get pod -l mon=rook-ceph-mon-a
```

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Name mgr and mds pods more consistently
PR description:
<!-- Please take a look at our [Contributing](https://rook.io/docs/rook/master/development-flow.html)
documentation before submitting a Pull Request!
Thank you for contributing to Rook! -->

The naming of the deployments and pods will now be more correlated with the ceph daemon names when troubleshooting the ceph cluster.
- The name of the mgr is now `rook-ceph-mgr` instead of `rook-ceph-mgr0`. There is only ever one of them.
- The name of the mds daemon is now the entire suffix of the pod instead of just the last suffix. For example, if the pod name is `rook-ceph-mds-myfs-7b9c79f684-h7dqj`, the mds daemon name would be `myfs-7b9c79f684-h7dqj` as seen in `ceph -s`, instead of `h7dqj`.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #2021: "rbd map" hangs in toolbox

Issue description:
As stated in the [docs](https://rook.io/docs/rook/v0.8/direct-tools.html), `rbd map` hangs (while still succeeding) when running it in the toolbox:
```sh
# Map the rbd device. If this command appears to hang, ctrl-c and check if it actually completed successfully by continuing.
rbd map replicapool/test
```

Because I was a bit annoyed by this, I decided to look into it. With a bit of help from #ceph-devel on IRC, I found that, after mapping the block image, "rbd map" [waits for an udev add event](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/blob/master/src/krbd.cc#L182-L251) for the /dev/rbd*X* block device. Using `udev monitor` inside the toolbox I noticed it didn't receive those events (while `udev monitor` on the host was receiving them). Googling around, I [found out](https://dummdida.tumblr.com/post/121087781445/re-udev-events-in-a-container) that the only way to get a container to receive udev events is to run the container with `--net=host`. Changing https://github.com/rook/rook/blame/master/Documentation/toolbox.md#L47 to `hostNetwork: true` fixed the hanging issue.

So, my suggestion is to change `hostNetwork: true` in the toolbox documentation (maybe with a comment that setting it to `false` will make `rbd map` hang), and refine the already existing hang comment. If you agree, I can create a PR.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

Successful build

Jenkins

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #1636: CRD handling prevents updating the number of mons

Issue description:
The operator has already implemented the ability to change the number of mons in the quorum. During the health checks, if more mons are desired, one will be added at a time. If fewer mons are desired, one at a time will be removed until we reach the desired state.

When the `monCount` is updated in the cluster CRD, the operator logs the message that the update is not supported. Restarting the operator may get past this, but usually will show the same error in the log.
```
update event for cluster rook is not supported
```

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Allow mons to scale up or down
PR description:
<!-- Please take a look at our [Contributing](https://rook.io/docs/rook/master/development-flow.html)
documentation before submitting a Pull Request!
Thank you for contributing to Rook! -->

**Description of your changes:**
The number of mons in the cluster can be changed by updating the `mon.count` in the cluster CRD. For example:
- When changed from 3 to 5, the operator will start two more mons.
- When changed from 5 to 3, the operator will remove two mons.

The mons will be added or removed by the periodic health check of the mons (every 45s by default). Since the CRD is applied in a different goroutine from the health check, there is a mutex to protect updating the number of mons. Note that once there are two or more mons, the operator cannot reduce the mon count below two because a quorum of two cannot remove a member.
